links.note_zh: 接下來：音樂的種類，先從西洋古典音樂的四百年開始。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The instrument shapes and the sounds are our own simplified drawings and recipes; the five-note pitches and the tune are covered by automatic tests.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的名稱、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；樂器的形狀與聲音是我們自己的簡化圖形與配方；五音的音高與旋律有自動測試。

sources.en: A 20th-century development, modeled on a Western symphony orchestra but using Chinese instruments; developed out of Jiangnan sizhu in the 1920s; four sections grouped by the way they are played; Great Unity Music Society 1921; the BCC Chinese Orchestra (1935) moved to Taiwan in 1949; in Taiwan guoyuetuan
sources.zh: 二十世紀發展出來的、以西洋交響樂團為模型但用中國樂器的樂團；1920 年代從江南絲竹發展；依演奏方式分四組；1921 年大同樂會；1935 年中央廣播電臺國樂團 1949 年遷台；台灣稱國樂團
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Chinese orchestra” and zh.wikipedia 中樂團

sources.en: The modern Chinese orchestra is generally divided into the four groups blow, bow, pluck, strike; called guoyuetuan in Taiwan; traditional sizhu ensembles are mostly pentatonic
sources.zh: 現代中樂團編制，一般分為吹、拉、彈、打四組；台灣稱國樂團；傳統絲竹合奏以五聲音階為主

sources.en: A two-stringed bowed instrument, a spike fiddle; python skin on the front of the sound box; the bow hair passes between the strings; no fingerboard; the strings are a fifth apart; evolved from the xiqin
sources.zh: 兩條弦的拉弦樂器；音箱前端蒙蟒皮；弓毛從兩條弦之間穿過；沒有指板；兩條弦相隔五度；由奚琴演變而來

sources.en: A bowed instrument with two strings, often tuned a fifth apart; a hexagonal or octagonal sound box covered with python skin; a bamboo bow strung with horsehair that passes between the two strings
sources.zh: 擦弦樂器；兩條弦，常以五度定弦；琴筒多呈六角或八角形，蒙以蟒皮；竹製弓桿，張以馬尾，穿於兩弦之間演奏
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「二胡」

sources.en: Belongs to the plucked category; pear-shaped wooden body; almost two thousand years in China; the pear-shaped pipa is likely to have been introduced from Central Asia; “pí” strike outward, “pá” pluck inward
sources.zh: 屬於彈撥類；半梨形木製音箱；在中國將近兩千年；半梨形的琵琶很可能從中亞傳入；「pí」向外彈、「pá」向內挑

sources.en: A plucked instrument; in the fourth century the pear-shaped, four-string, four-fret pipa came to the Central Plains from the western regions
sources.zh: 彈撥樂器；西元四世紀，西域文化交流，致使半梨形音箱、四弦四柱的琵琶傳入中原
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「琵琶」

sources.en: A Chinese transverse flute; bangdi, qudi, xindi; a membrane hole (mo kong) between the embouchure and finger holes; the dimo makes the tone brighter and louder with a buzzing, nasal quality; the dizi as we know it dates roughly to the 5th century BC
sources.zh: 中國橫笛；梆笛、曲笛、新笛；吹孔與按音孔之間有膜孔；笛膜讓聲音更亮、更大聲，帶嗡嗡的鼻音質感；我們知道的笛，大約出現在西元前五世紀

sources.en: Bangdi: bamboo, played sideways, one blow hole, one membrane hole, six finger holes; dimo: the thin membrane on the membrane hole, enlarging the volume and making the tone clear and bright; di: a blown instrument, a bamboo-class instrument of the eight sounds, mostly played sideways
sources.zh: 梆笛：竹製，橫吹，一個吹孔、一個膜孔、六個按音孔；笛膜：貼於膜孔上的薄膜，有擴大音量並使音色清脆明亮的作用；笛：吹管樂器，古代屬八音的竹類樂器，多為橫吹
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「梆笛」「笛膜」「笛」

sources.en: Drum: a percussion instrument, hide stretched over a hollow wooden body, struck with the hands, sticks, or mallets; gong: a shallow flat bronze disc struck with a mallet
sources.zh: 鼓：打擊樂器，用皮革蒙在中空木桶上所製成，常以手、木棒或鼓槌擊奏；鑼：銅製的淺平圓盤，用槌敲擊
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「鼓」「鑼」

sources.en: The guqin is a plucked seven-string instrument; not the guzheng, which has moveable bridges; originally five strings for gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu; the most common tuning is pentatonic; 古箏 traditionally arranged in a pentatonic scale, 21 to 25 strings
sources.zh: 古琴是彈撥的七弦樂器；不是有可移動琴馬的古箏；傳說原本五條弦代表宮商角徵羽；最常見的定弦是五聲音階；古箏傳統上按五聲音階排列，21 到 25 條弦
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Guqin” and 教育部辭典「古琴」「古箏」

sources.en: The five notes gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu, also called the five sounds
sources.zh: 宮、商、角、徵、羽五個音階，也稱為「五聲」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「五音」

sources.en: The eight sounds: an ancient classification by material: metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, clay, hide, wood
sources.zh: 古代依製作材料分為金、石、絲、竹、匏、土、革、木等八類
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「八音」

sources.en: Ancient music popular in Fujian, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia since the Song and Yuan; the singer holds clappers; accompaniment led by the pipa, with dongxiao, sanxian, erxian, and clappers
sources.zh: 宋元以後流行於福建、臺灣及東南亞地區的古樂；歌者執拍板，伴奏以琵琶為主，再配洞簫、三弦、二弦、四塊板
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「南管」

sources.en: Nanguan came to Taiwan during the Ming dynasty and became popular in Lukang; pipa played across the lap; inscribed by UNESCO in 2009; beiguan was widespread in Taiwan, with suona, bangzi, gongs, drums, and cymbals
sources.zh: 南管在明代傳到台灣、在鹿港很盛行；琵琶橫抱彈奏；2009 年被聯合國教科文組織列入；北管曾在台灣很盛行，用嗩吶、梆子、鑼、鼓和鈸

sources.en: Beiguan is a traditional music of the Han people in Taiwan; arrived about the Qianlong–Jiaqing years; the most guanges are in Changhua and Yilan; most street bands are beiguan bands; no theatrical form related to beiguan exists in Fujian today
sources.zh: 北管為臺灣漢族傳統音樂；大約在清朝乾隆、嘉慶年間傳入；以彰化與宜蘭的館閣最多；大多數音樂陣頭為北管樂團；在今日福建省卻無與北管音樂相關的劇種

sources.en: The Taipei Chinese Orchestra was founded in 1979, the first professional Chinese orchestra in Taiwan; the National Chinese Orchestra Taiwan began in 1984 as an experimental orchestra at the National Taiwan Academy of the Arts and was renamed in 2012
sources.zh: 臺北市立國樂團創立於 1979 年，是臺灣第一個專業國樂團；臺灣國樂團前身為 1984 年成立的國立藝專實驗國樂團，2012 年更名
sources.src: zh.wikipedia 臺北市立國樂團、臺灣國樂團

sources.en: Taiwan's 12-year curriculum: arts (music) 音 E-Ⅱ-2, 音 E-Ⅲ-2, 音 A-Ⅲ-1, 音 A-Ⅳ-1
sources.zh: 十二年國民基本教育課程綱要藝術領域：音 E-Ⅱ-2、音 E-Ⅲ-2、音 A-Ⅲ-1、音 A-Ⅳ-1
sources.src: 國家教育研究院，十二年國教藝術領域課綱

sources.en: Safe listening: headphone volume to 60% of maximum, personal audio devices less than one hour a day
sources.zh: 安全聆聽：耳機音量不超過最大的 60%、個人音響裝置每天少於一小時

units.blurb_en: Western classical music, jazz, the music that grew in Taiwan, Buddhist chanting, and how a song is put together.
units.blurb_zh: 西洋古典音樂、爵士樂、台灣這塊土地上長出來的音樂、梵唄，以及一首歌是怎麼組成的。

lessons.title: How Did Western Music Change Over 400 Years?
lessons.title_zh: 西洋古典音樂四百年怎麼變？
lessons.blurb_en: Hear one short tune written three ways: Baroque, Classical, and Romantic. See the notes, the loudness, and the tempo, and learn to hear which style is which.
lessons.blurb_zh: 聽同一段短旋律用三種寫法：巴洛克、古典和浪漫。看音符、力度和速度，學會聽出哪一種是哪一種。
lessons.big_idea_en: Music is written differently in different times. The same tune can get a different accompaniment, loudness, and tempo, and that is a big part of what the names Baroque, Classical, and Romantic point to.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 不同的時代，音樂的寫法不同。同一段旋律可以有不同的伴奏、力度和速度，而這正是「巴洛克」「古典」「浪漫」這些名稱主要指的東西。

lab.how_en: We wrote one short tune of four bars. Choose a period and press play. The gold notes are the tune, and they stay exactly the same. The teal notes are the accompaniment, and the purple line is the loudness. The three versions are our own simple imitations of typical features, not real pieces from those periods. Switch on “Tune only” to check that the tune does not change.
lab.how_zh: 我們寫了一段四小節的短旋律。選一個時期，按播放。金色的音是旋律，完全不變。青綠色的音是伴奏，紫色的線是力度。這三個版本是我們依典型特徵做的簡單模仿，不是那些時期的真曲子。打開「只聽旋律」，檢查旋律有沒有變。

baroque.en: A continuous bass line, called basso continuo, with a chord instrument such as a harpsichord or organ.
baroque.zh: 不停的低音，叫通奏低音（持續低音），由大鍵琴或管風琴等能彈和弦的樂器擔任。

baroque.en: Loudness changes in steps: piano, then forte. This is called terraced dynamics, and a harpsichord cannot vary its loudness by touch.
baroque.zh: 力度一階一階地換：弱，然後強。這叫階梯式力度；大鍵琴不能用手指的力道改變音量。

baroque.en: Ornaments, such as trills and mordents, were often added by the performers. We add one short ornament.
baroque.zh: 裝飾音，例如顫音與迴音，常由演奏者自己加上。我們加了一個短短的裝飾音。

baroque.en: Our own simplification: short, bright, plucked-sounding notes, as on a harpsichord.
baroque.zh: 我們自己的簡化：短而亮、像撥出來的音，像大鍵琴。

classical.en: A clear melody over a subordinate chordal accompaniment: a lighter, clearer texture.
classical.zh: 一條清楚的旋律，在比較次要的和弦伴奏上面：比較輕、比較清楚的織度。

classical.en: Alberti bass: the notes of the chord in the order lowest, highest, middle, highest.
classical.zh: 阿貝提低音：和弦的音依「最低、最高、中間、最高」的順序彈。

classical.en: Balanced phrases that are brief, typically four bars long. Our tune is one four-bar phrase.
classical.zh: 平衡的樂句，很短，通常是四小節。我們的旋律就是一個四小節的樂句。

classical.en: The piano, or fortepiano, replaced the harpsichord as the main keyboard instrument. The smooth swell in loudness is our own choice.
classical.zh: 鋼琴（或古鋼琴）取代了大鍵琴，成為主要的鍵盤樂器。力度平順的起伏是我們自己的選擇。

romantic.en: A wider range of dynamics, for example from ppp to fff.
romantic.zh: 更寬的力度範圍，例如從 ppp 到 fff。

romantic.en: Increased chromaticism: harmony that uses more notes from outside the key. We borrow one chord from the minor key.
romantic.zh: 更多的半音化：和聲用更多調外的音。我們借了一個小調的和弦。

romantic.en: Rubato, a slight speeding up and then slowing down of the tempo, for expression. The word is older than the Romantic era.
romantic.zh: 彈性速度：為了表情，稍微加快、再放慢。這個詞比浪漫時期還早。

romantic.en: Individual, emotional, dramatic music, and a modern piano with a more powerful, sustained tone. The wide arpeggios are our own simplification.
romantic.zh: 個人的、情感的、戲劇性的音樂，與音量更大、延音更長的現代鋼琴。寬廣的分解和弦是我們自己的簡化。

paras: The words “classical music” can mean all of the Western art music tradition, from the Middle Ages to today. But there is also a narrower Classical period. In this lesson we look at three periods that are often named: the Baroque, roughly 1600 to 1750, the Classical, roughly 1750 to 1820, and the Romantic, roughly the nineteenth century. The dates are only approximate, and the books disagree about them.

Much Baroque music has a basso continuo: a bass line that keeps going, played by a bass instrument together with an instrument that can play chords, such as a harpsichord or an organ. Performers often added ornaments, such as trills and mordents. A harpsichord cannot change its loudness by how hard you press the key, so the dynamics were often terraced, a step from piano to forte. But not all of it: later composers, such as Vivaldi, used more varied dynamics.

Classical music tends to have a lighter, clearer texture. It is mainly homophonic, with a clear melody over a chordal accompaniment. The phrases are balanced and brief, typically four bars long. A common accompaniment is the Alberti bass, which plays the notes of a chord in the order lowest, highest, middle, highest. The symphony and the string quartet became prominent, and the piano gradually replaced the harpsichord.

Romantic composers sought to make music that was individual, emotional, and dramatic. They used a wider range of dynamics, for example from ppp to fff, and more chromatic harmony. The orchestra grew, with as many as 120 players for the works of Wagner and Mahler. The modern piano, with its more powerful and more sustained tone, took over from the fortepiano. And the inspiration was not only love: it could be nature, literature, or poetry.

The periods overlap, and many composers do not fit just one. Bach (1685–1750) is a late Baroque composer. Mozart (1756–1791) is a Classical composer. Chopin (1810–1849) is an early Romantic composer. Beethoven (1770–1827) was mentored during the Classical period, and his style was a key driver of the transition to Romantic music. Schubert (1797–1828) belongs to the late Classical and early Romantic eras.

The tune on this page is our own, and the three versions are only teaching imitations of some typical features. Real composers varied a great deal. One musicologist points out that there is too much diversity within the music of the time to make sweeping generalizations. So treat the names as helpful handles, and listen to real music with open ears.
paras_zh: 「古典音樂」這幾個字，可以指整個西方藝術音樂的傳統，從中世紀到今天。但也有比較窄的「古典時期」。這一課我們看三個常被提到的時期：巴洛克，大約 1600 到 1750 年；古典，大約 1750 到 1820 年；浪漫，大約是十九世紀。年代只是約略的，各書的說法也不一樣。
許多巴洛克音樂有通奏低音：一條不停的低音，由低音樂器和一件能彈和弦的樂器（例如大鍵琴或管風琴）一起演奏。演奏者常常加上裝飾音，例如顫音和迴音。大鍵琴不能用按鍵的力道改變音量，所以力度常常是階梯式的，從弱一階跳到強。但不是全部：後來的作曲家，例如韋瓦第，用了更多變化的力度。
古典音樂的織度比較輕、比較清楚。它主要是主音音樂（homophony）：一條清楚的旋律，在和弦的伴奏之上。樂句平衡而短，通常是四小節。常見的伴奏是阿貝提低音，把和弦的音依「最低、最高、中間、最高」的順序彈。交響曲和弦樂四重奏變得重要，鋼琴也逐漸取代了大鍵琴。
浪漫時期的作曲家想寫個人的、情感的、戲劇性的音樂。他們用更寬的力度範圍，例如從 ppp 到 fff，與更半音化的和聲。樂團變大了，華格納與馬勒的作品用到多達 120 位演奏者。現代鋼琴音量更大、延音更長，取代了古鋼琴。而靈感不只是愛情：可以是自然、文學或詩。
這些時期互相重疊，許多作曲家也不只屬於一個。巴哈（1685–1750）是巴洛克晚期的作曲家。莫札特（1756–1791）是古典時期的作曲家。蕭邦（1810–1849）是早期浪漫的作曲家。貝多芬（1770–1827）在古典時期受教，他的風格是推動轉向浪漫音樂的關鍵。舒伯特（1797–1828）屬於古典晚期與浪漫早期。
這一頁的旋律是我們自己寫的，三個版本只是對一些典型特徵的教學式模仿。真正的作曲家變化很大。一位音樂學者指出，那個時代的音樂內部差異太大，不能一概而論。所以把這些名稱當作方便的把手，然後用開放的耳朵去聽真正的音樂。
questions: What is an Alberti bass?
Why were Baroque dynamics often “terraced”?
Why is Beethoven hard to put in just one period?
answers: An accompaniment figure that plays the notes of a chord in the order lowest, highest, middle, highest. It is often used in the Classical era.
A harpsichord cannot vary its loudness by touch, so a change in loudness came as a step, from piano to forte. But later Baroque composers used more varied dynamics.
He was mentored in the Classical period, and his style drove the transition to Romantic music. Some call him a transitional composer.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It · 動手試試

parts.text_en: Watch the loudness curve: it drops in one step in the third bar.
parts.text_zh: 看力度曲線：在第三小節一階掉下去。

parts.text_en: The teal notes underneath go low, high, middle, high, again and again.
parts.text_zh: 下面青綠色的音一直重複 低、高、中、高。

parts.text_en: The piece slows down at the ends of phrases, and the notes cover the widest range.
parts.text_zh: 樂曲在句尾放慢，音的範圍最寬。

parts.text_en: Switch on “Tune only” and play all three. The gold notes are the same each time.
parts.text_zh: 打開「只聽旋律」，三個都播一次。金色的音每次都一樣。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the game below: can you tell the three styles apart without looking?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試下面的遊戲：不看畫面，你分得出三種寫法嗎？

eraq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays our tune in one of the three styles. Choose which one. If you cannot hear the sound, press “What is in the music” to read what the music is doing.
eraq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題用三種寫法之一播放我們的旋律。選出是哪一種。如果聽不到聲音，按「音樂裡有什麼」，讀一讀音樂在做什麼。

timeline.lead_en: The three periods overlap, and the books give different dates. Here are the dates that the sources gave.
timeline.lead_zh: 三個時期互相重疊，各書給的年代也不一樣。這裡是各來源給的年代。

items.note_en: About 1600 to 1750 (one page says 1580). The harpsichord is the main keyboard, and the orchestra is not yet standard.
items.note_zh: 約 1600 到 1750（有一頁寫 1580）。大鍵琴是主要的鍵盤，樂團還沒有標準化。

items.note_en: Roughly 1750 to 1820 (Taiwan’s NAER gives 1825). The piano replaces the harpsichord, and the orchestra is typically about 40.
items.note_zh: 約 1750 到 1820（國教院寫 1825）。鋼琴取代大鍵琴，樂團通常約 40 人。

items.note_en: From the early nineteenth century to the early twentieth (NAER gives 1820 to 1900). Orchestras grow, up to about 120 players.
items.note_zh: 從十九世紀初到二十世紀初（國教院寫 1820 到 1900）。樂團變大，多達約 120 人。

timeline.caveat_en: A short “galant” transition lies between the Baroque and the Classical, and Beethoven stands between the Classical and the Romantic. Boundaries like these are a convenience for us.
timeline.caveat_zh: 巴洛克與古典之間有一段短短的「加朗」過渡期，貝多芬站在古典與浪漫之間。這樣的界線，是為了方便我們。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The curriculum names composers and musical vocabulary, and, for senior high, music of different periods. The words Baroque and Romantic do not appear in the curriculum itself.
curric.lead_zh: 課綱寫到作曲家與音樂語彙，高中階段才寫到不同時期的音樂。「巴洛克」「浪漫」這些詞，課綱本文裡沒有出現。

items.text: 音樂元素，如：節奏、力度、速度等。
items.note_en: Dynamics and tempo are what change from style to style in this lesson.
items.note_zh: 這一課裡，隨寫法而變的就是力度和速度。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 器樂曲與聲樂曲，如：各國民謠、本土與傳統音樂、古典與流行音樂等，以及樂曲之作曲家、演奏者、傳統藝師與創作背景。
items.note_en: Classical music is named here, along with its composers and the background of a piece.
items.note_zh: 這裡寫到古典音樂，與樂曲的作曲家和創作背景。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 相關音樂語彙，如曲調、調式等描述音樂元素之音樂術語，或相關之一般性用語。
items.note_en: Words like these help us describe what we hear.
items.note_zh: 這樣的詞，幫助我們描述聽到的東西。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（高中）
items.text: 能使用適當的音樂語彙，賞析不同時期與地域的音樂作品，探索音樂與文化
items.note_en: Music of different periods and places is named in senior high school.
items.note_zh: 高中階段才寫到不同時期與地域的音樂作品。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A word with two meanings, a keyboard that changed, a bigger orchestra, and a bridge
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個有兩個意思的詞、一件改變的鍵盤、變大的樂團，和一座橋
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how Western music changed.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於西洋音樂怎麼變的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: In Taiwan’s dictionary, 古典音樂 has two senses. The first is art music rooted in the Western tradition, from about the eleventh century to the present. The second is the music of the Classical period, 1750 to 1820, valuing form, reason, and objectivity, and setting the model for the symphony, the sonata, and chamber music. So the word “classical” has to be read from the context.
cards.body_zh: 在台灣的辭典裡，「古典音樂」有兩個意思。第一個是根植於西方傳統的藝術音樂，從大約十一世紀直到現在。第二個是古典時期 1750 到 1820 年的音樂，注重形式、理性與客觀，建立了交響曲、奏鳴曲和室內樂的典範。所以「古典」這個詞，要看上下文才知道指哪一個。

cards.body_en: A harpsichord plucks its strings and gives no expressive control over individual notes. The piano can continuously vary dynamics by touch, so it slowly took over in the Classical period. In the nineteenth century a cast iron frame allowed much greater string tension, and the modern piano, with a more powerful and sustained tone, took over from the more delicate fortepiano. The harpsichord did not vanish at once: Classical composers still used it in concerts.
cards.body_zh: 大鍵琴是撥弦，對單一個音沒有表情的控制。鋼琴可以用手指力道連續改變力度，所以在古典時期慢慢取代了它。十九世紀，鑄鐵框讓弦可以承受大得多的張力，音量更大、延音更長的現代鋼琴，取代了比較纖細的古鋼琴。大鍵琴不是一下子消失的：古典時期的作曲家在音樂會上還是常常用它。

cards.k: A Bigger Orchestra · 變大的樂團
cards.zh: 從約 40 人到一百多人
cards.body_en: Baroque orchestras were not standardized: one orchestra of Bach had up to 18 players, while Corelli’s in Rome had between 35 and 80 for daily performances. The typical Classical orchestra was around 40. The size of the orchestra grew throughout the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, to as many as 120 players for Wagner and Mahler.
cards.body_zh: 巴洛克的樂團沒有標準：巴哈的一個樂團多達 18 位演奏者，而柯雷利在羅馬的樂團，平日演出有 35 到 80 位。古典時期的典型樂團大約 40 人。樂團的規模在十八和十九世紀不斷成長，到華格納和馬勒時，多達 120 位演奏者。

cards.body_en: Beethoven was mentored during the Classical period, and his musical style was a key driver of the transition to Romantic music. Some people count his Third Symphony as the first symphony of the Romantic era, though that is contested. Schubert, who was born in 1797, is also described as a composer of the late Classical and early Romantic eras. Real music does not stay in boxes.
cards.body_zh: 貝多芬在古典時期受教，他的音樂風格是推動轉向浪漫音樂的關鍵。有些人把他的第三號交響曲算成浪漫時期的第一首交響曲，不過這有爭議。1797 年出生的舒伯特，也被描述為古典晚期與浪漫早期的作曲家。真正的音樂不會待在盒子裡。

myths.myth_en: Baroque music ended exactly in 1750, when Bach died.
myths.myth_zh: 巴洛克音樂在 1750 年巴哈去世時剛好結束。
myths.fact_en: 1750 is a convenient end date. The sources admit appreciable disagreement, and there was a short transition, the galant style, in between.
myths.fact_zh: 1750 只是方便的結束年份。資料承認各家的說法有明顯的差異，中間還有一段短短的過渡期，「加朗」風格。

myths.myth_en: “Classical music” means only the music of Mozart’s time.
myths.myth_zh: 「古典音樂」只指莫札特那個時代的音樂。
myths.fact_en: The term can include all Western art music. The narrower Classical period is roughly 1750 to 1820.
myths.fact_zh: 這個詞可以包括所有西方藝術音樂。比較窄的古典時期，大約是 1750 到 1820 年。

myths.myth_en: Romantic music is all about love.
myths.myth_zh: 浪漫音樂都是在寫愛情。
myths.fact_en: It is often inspired by nature, literature, poetry, or the fine arts. “Romantic” here is tied to the Romanticism movement, not only to romance.
myths.fact_zh: 它常常受自然、文學、詩或美術啟發。這裡的「浪漫」連著浪漫主義這場運動，不只是愛情。

myths.myth_en: Rubato was invented by the Romantic composers.
myths.myth_zh: 彈性速度是浪漫時期的作曲家發明的。
myths.fact_en: The term rubato existed even before the Romantic era. Romantic players used it a great deal for expression.
myths.fact_zh: 「rubato」這個詞在浪漫時期之前就有了。浪漫時期的演奏者為了表情，用得很多。

tricks.title_en: Baroque: a bass that never stops
tricks.body_en: Basso continuo, ornaments, steps in loudness.
tricks.body_zh: 通奏低音、裝飾音、力度一階一階。

tricks.body_en: Melody over chords, short phrases, Alberti bass.
tricks.body_zh: 旋律在和弦上、短樂句、阿貝提低音。

tricks.body_en: Big dynamics, more chromatic harmony, rubato.
tricks.body_zh: 大的力度、更半音化的和聲、彈性速度。

tricks.body_en: Composers do not stay in boxes.
tricks.body_zh: 作曲家不會待在盒子裡。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The Romantic version gets much louder in the middle.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。浪漫的版本在中間會變得大聲很多。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: In a concert hall, you may hear very loud passages. If something is too loud, covering your ears for a moment is fine.
safety.zh: 在音樂廳裡，你可能會聽到非常響的段落。如果太大聲，暫時摀住耳朵也沒關係。

activities.title_en: Three Ways to Play One Tune

materials.en: A simple tune everyone knows, such as a short nursery song
materials.zh: 大家都會的簡單旋律，例如一首短短的童謠

materials.en: A keyboard or xylophone, or just voices and clapping
materials.zh: 鍵盤或木琴，或只用聲音和拍手

steps.en: Play or sing the tune plainly, one time. Everyone listens.
steps.zh: 平平地彈或唱一次旋律。大家聽。

steps.en: Version 1: play every note short and bright, and play the loudness in steps: loud, loud, soft, soft.
steps.zh: 版本一：每個音彈得短而亮，力度一階一階：大聲、大聲、小聲、小聲。

steps.en: Version 2: add a steady pattern underneath: low, high, middle, high. Make the loudness grow and fade smoothly.
steps.zh: 版本二：下面加一個穩定的圖樣：低、高、中、高。讓力度平順地漸強再漸弱。

steps.en: Version 3: play slowly, slow down at the end of each phrase, and make big swings from very soft to very loud.
steps.zh: 版本三：慢慢彈，每個樂句結尾放慢，從很弱到很強，大幅度地起伏。

steps.en: Talk about it: which one felt the most like a story? Which was the most tidy? Why?
steps.zh: 討論：哪一個最像在說故事？哪一個最整齊？為什麼？

activities.tip_en: There is no right answer for how each one feels. Let students use their own words.
activities.tip_zh: 每一個版本給人的感覺沒有標準答案。讓學生用自己的話說。

materials.en: A long strip of paper
materials.zh: 一長條紙

materials.en: Colored pens
materials.zh: 彩色筆

materials.en: The timeline on this page
materials.zh: 本頁的時間軸

steps.en: Mark the years 1600, 1700, 1800, and 1900 along the strip.
Draw the three periods as colored bars. Let them overlap where the sources disagree.
steps.zh: 把三個時期畫成彩色長條。各來源不同的地方，讓它們重疊。

steps.en: Add the composers from this page with their years of birth and death.
steps.zh: 把本頁的作曲家和他們的生卒年加上去。

steps.en: Ask: who lived in two periods? What changed in the instruments and the orchestra?
steps.zh: 問：誰橫跨兩個時期？樂器和樂團改變了什麼？

activities.tip_en: Let students argue about where to draw the lines. That is the point.
activities.tip_zh: 讓學生為界線畫在哪裡爭論。那就是重點。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The tune and the three versions are our own teaching imitations, and their rhythm, loudness, and harmony are covered by automatic tests.

sources.en: The period or dominant style of Western classical music composed from about 1600 to 1750; appreciable disagreement about time boundaries; extensive ornamentation, typically improvised, such as trills and mordents; the harpsichord was the pre-eminent keyboard instrument; a short transition (the galant style)
sources.zh: 約 1600 到 1750 年作曲的西方古典音樂的時期或主流風格；時間界線有明顯的分歧；大量裝飾音，通常即興，例如顫音與迴音；大鍵琴是最重要的鍵盤樂器；一段短短的過渡（加朗風格）

sources.en: Basso continuo is a harmonic structure almost universal in the Baroque era; at least one chord instrument such as a harpsichord or organ, and bass instruments; terraced dynamics is the alternation of piano and forte; later Baroque musicians such as Vivaldi used more varied dynamics
sources.zh: 通奏低音是巴洛克時期幾乎普遍的和聲結構；至少一件能彈和弦的樂器，如大鍵琴或管風琴，加上低音樂器；階梯式力度是弱與強的交替；後來的巴洛克音樂家如韋瓦第用了更多變化的力度

sources.en: An era of classical music between roughly 1750 and 1820; a lighter, clearer texture than the Baroque; mainly homophonic; balanced phrases, typically four bars; symphony and string quartet; the harpsichord was superseded by the piano; composers more often indicated ornaments
sources.zh: 約 1750 到 1820 年的古典音樂時代；織度比巴洛克更輕、更清楚；主要是主音音樂；平衡的樂句，通常四小節；交響曲與弦樂四重奏；大鍵琴被鋼琴取代；作曲家更常標出裝飾音

sources.en: An accompaniment figure often used in the Classical era, in which the notes of the chord are presented in the order lowest, highest, middle, highest
sources.zh: 古典時期常用的伴奏型態，和弦的音依最低、最高、中間、最高的順序出現

sources.en: Composers sought music that was individualistic, emotional, dramatic, and often programmatic; a wider range of dynamics, for example from ppp to fff; increased chromaticism; inspired by nature, literature, poetry, super-natural elements, or the fine arts; large, grand orchestras
sources.zh: 作曲家想要個人的、情感的、戲劇性的、常常標題性的音樂；更寬的力度範圍，如 ppp 到 fff；更多半音化；受自然、文學、詩、超自然或美術啟發；大型、宏偉的樂團

sources.en: The term classical music includes all Western art music from the medieval era to the 21st century; the Classical era is the 1750s to the early 1820s; the Romantic era from roughly the first decade of the 19th century to the early 20th century; the modern piano took over from the fortepiano; Beethoven as a transitional composer
sources.zh: 「古典音樂」包括從中世紀到二十一世紀的所有西方藝術音樂；古典時期是 1750 年代到 1820 年代初；浪漫時期約從十九世紀的第一個十年到二十世紀初；現代鋼琴取代了古鋼琴；貝多芬是過渡的作曲家

sources.en: Expressive and rhythmic freedom by a slight speeding up and then slowing down of the tempo; the term existed even before the Romantic era
sources.zh: 藉由稍微加快、再放慢速度而得到的表情與節奏的自由；這個詞在浪漫時期之前就有了

sources.en: The harpsichord offers no dynamic or expressive control over individual notes; the piano can continuously vary dynamics by touch; the cast iron frame allowed much greater string tensions
sources.zh: 大鍵琴對單一個音沒有力度或表情的控制；鋼琴可以用手指力道連續改變力度；鑄鐵框讓弦可以承受大得多的張力

sources.en: The orchestra grew in size throughout the 18th and 19th centuries; as many as 120 players for Wagner and later Mahler; in the Baroque era the size and composition were not standardised; Bach had up to 18 players at Koethen
sources.zh: 樂團在十八、十九世紀不斷成長；華格納與後來的馬勒多達 120 位；巴洛克時期的規模與編制沒有標準化；巴哈在克滕有多達 18 位演奏者

sources.en: Beethoven was mentored during the Classical period, and his style was a key driver of the transition to Romantic music; born 1770 (baptised 17 December 1770), died 1827; Schubert was an Austrian composer of the late Classical and early Romantic eras
sources.zh: 貝多芬在古典時期受教，他的風格是轉向浪漫音樂的關鍵；1770 年出生（12 月 17 日受洗），1827 年去世；舒伯特是古典晚期與浪漫早期的奧地利作曲家

sources.src: Wikipedia, composer pages: Bach, Mozart, Chopin

sources.en: Sense 2: the music of the classicist period, 1750–1820, valuing form, reason, and objectivity, and setting the model for the symphony, sonata, and chamber music; sense 1: art music rooted in the Western tradition, from about the eleventh century to the present
sources.zh: 2. 指西元 1750～1820 年古典主義時期的音樂，其特色為注重形式、理性與客觀，建立了交響曲、奏鳴曲及室內樂等的典範；1. 泛指根植於西方音樂傳統的藝術音樂，包含了從大約十一世紀直至當代的廣大時間範圍
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「古典音樂」

sources.en: Harpsichord: a mechanism plucks the strings instead of striking them; replaced by the piano after the 18th century. Symphony: established by Haydn after the mid-18th century and expanded by Beethoven. Romantic school: popular in the 19th century, showing individuality, self, and unrestrained emotion
sources.zh: 大鍵琴: 利用機械裝置撥動琴弦，而非機械敲擊；十八世紀後漸為鋼琴所取代。交響曲: 十八世紀中葉後由海頓所奠立，貝多芬逐漸擴充發展。浪漫樂派: 流行於十九世紀，以展現個性、自我、無拘無束的情感為主
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「大鍵琴」「交響曲」「浪漫樂派」

lessons.title: What Makes Jazz Sound Like Jazz?
lessons.title_zh: 爵士樂為什麼聽起來像爵士？
lessons.blurb_en: Slide one number and watch every off-beat note move later. Hear the same tune straight and swung, and play along with a small band.
lessons.blurb_zh: 拖動一個數字，看每個反拍的音往後移。聽同一段旋律平均和搖擺的差別，再跟一個小樂隊即興。
lessons.big_idea_en: Swing comes from dividing each beat unevenly: the first eighth note is longer and the second is shorter. The beat itself stays steady.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 搖擺來自不平均地切每一拍：前面的八分音符變長、後面的變短。拍子本身還是穩定的。

lab.how_en: We wrote one short tune of four bars, with a simple bass line and a hi-hat. Press play, then drag the swing ratio. The orange notes are the off-beat eighth notes: they are the only ones that move. The tempo and the pitches never change. This is our own simple model, not a recording of any jazz band.
lab.how_zh: 我們寫了一段四小節的短旋律，加上簡單的低音和 hi-hat（踩鈸）。按播放，再拖動搖擺比例。橘色的是反拍的八分音符：只有它們會移動。速度和音高都不會變。這是我們自己的簡單模型，不是任何爵士樂團的錄音。

paras: Jazz is a music genre that originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans, Louisiana, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. But jazz did not begin as a single musical tradition in New Orleans or elsewhere. It is difficult to define, because it includes a wide range of music. Jazz is characterized by swing and blue notes, complex chords, call and response, polyrhythms, and improvisation.

In swing rhythm the pulse is divided unequally. The first note of each pair of eighth notes is lengthened, and the second is shortened. The first note is often understood to be twice as long as the second, a triplet feel, a ratio of 2:1. But in practice the ratio is often much more subtle. In jazz, the swing ratio typically lies somewhere between 1:1 and 3:1, and can vary considerably. It tends to be wider at slower tempos and narrower at faster ones.

A typical jazz group has a rhythm section, which provides the underlying rhythm, harmony, and pulse. The standard rhythm section is piano, bass, and drums. A soloist, or a horn section of woodwinds and brass, plays the melody on top. The bass often plays a walking bass line: unsyncopated notes of equal value, usually quarter notes, like the regular steps of someone walking.

Improvisation is one of jazz’s defining elements. Jazz improvisation is the spontaneous invention of melodic solo lines or accompaniment parts in a performance. It is usually done over a chord progression, so it is not random. For example, the twelve-bar blues is based on the I, IV, and V chords of a key. And not all jazz is improvised: swing-era big bands relied more on arrangements that were written or memorized, and the soloists improvised within them.

Two more ingredients are blue notes and call and response. A blue note is sung or played at a slightly different pitch from standard, typically between a quartertone and a semitone. Call and response is a succession of two distinct phrases that works like a conversation in music: one musician offers a phrase, and a second answers. Syncopation places rhythmic stresses where they would not normally occur.

The tune and the band on this page are our own simple model, built to show one idea. Real players vary a great deal, and not all jazz swings: free jazz explored playing without regular meter or beat. Louis Armstrong (1901–1971) and Duke Ellington (1899–1974) are two of its famous figures. Ellington once said of the music, “It’s all music.”
paras_zh: 爵士樂是十九世紀末到二十世紀初，在美國路易斯安那州紐奧良的非裔美國人社群中形成的音樂類型。但爵士樂並不是從紐奧良或別處的某一個傳統開始的。它很難定義，因為它包含很廣的音樂。爵士樂的特色是搖擺與藍調音、複雜的和弦、呼應（call and response）、多重節奏，以及即興。
在搖擺的節奏裡，脈動被不平均地切開。每一對八分音符的前一個被拉長，後一個被縮短。人們常把前一個理解成後一個的兩倍長，也就是三連音的感覺，比例 2:1。但實際上，比例常常細微得多。在爵士樂裡，搖擺比例通常落在 1:1 到 3:1 之間，變化很大。速度慢時比例傾向變大，速度快時傾向變小。
一個典型的爵士樂團有節奏組，提供底下的節奏、和聲與脈動。標準的節奏組是鋼琴、貝斯和鼓。獨奏者，或是由木管與銅管組成的管樂組，在上面演奏旋律。貝斯常常彈行走低音（walking bass）：沒有切分、音值相等的音，通常是四分音符，像一個人規律的腳步。
即興是爵士樂的決定性元素之一。爵士即興是在演出中，當場創造旋律的獨奏線條或伴奏聲部。它通常在和弦進行上進行，所以不是亂彈。例如十二小節藍調，是建立在一個調的 I、IV、V 和弦上。而且不是所有爵士樂都是即興的：搖擺時代的大樂團比較倚賴寫好或背熟的編曲，獨奏者在編曲裡即興。
另外兩個要素是藍調音與呼應。藍調音是用和標準音高稍微不同的音高唱或奏出，通常相差四分之一音到一個半音之間。呼應是兩個不同樂句相連，像音樂裡的對話：一位樂手提出一個樂句，另一位回答。切分音是把節奏的重音放在平常不會出現的地方。
這一頁的旋律和樂隊是我們自己的簡單模型，用來展示一個想法。真正的樂手變化很大，也不是所有爵士樂都搖擺：自由爵士探索沒有規則拍子與節拍的演奏。路易斯・阿姆斯壯（1901–1971）和艾靈頓公爵（1899–1974）是它著名的人物。艾靈頓曾說到這種音樂：「這全是音樂。」
questions: What does “swing” do to a pair of eighth notes?
Is jazz improvisation random?
Does every jazz piece swing?
answers: It lengthens the first note and shortens the second. The beat itself stays steady.
No. It is usually done over a chord progression, so it follows the harmony.
No. Free jazz explored playing without regular meter or beat.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It · 動手試試

parts.text_en: Each beat is split into two equal halves. The orange notes sit exactly on the dashed lines.
parts.text_zh: 每一拍切成兩個一樣長的一半。橘色的音剛好落在虛線上。

parts.text_en: A small step toward swing. In real playing the ratio is often much more subtle than a triplet.
parts.text_zh: 往搖擺走一小步。實際演奏時，比例常常比三連音細微得多。

parts.text_en: The first eighth note is twice as long as the second. This is how swing is often understood.
parts.text_zh: 前面的八分音符是後面的兩倍長。這是人們常用來理解搖擺的方式。

parts.text_en: The upper end of the range that the sources give. The off-beat notes come very late.
parts.text_zh: 來源給的範圍的上緣。反拍的音來得很晚。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the two games below: tell straight from swung, and play along with the band.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試下面兩個遊戲：分辨平均與搖擺，再跟樂隊一起即興。

swingq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays our tune at one tempo. Choose whether the eighth notes are straight or swung. If you cannot hear the sound, press “What is in the music”.
swingq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題用一個速度播放我們的旋律。選出八分音符是平均的，還是搖擺的。如果聽不到聲音，按「音樂裡有什麼」。

improv.lead_en: The band plays only bass and hi-hat. Tap notes from a five-note scale (lesson 7). Your notes are placed on the grid of eighth notes, straight or swung. Then play your phrase back.
improv.lead_zh: 樂隊只有低音和 hi-hat。點五聲音階（第七課）的音。你的音會被貼到八分音符的格子上，平均的或搖擺的。再播放你的樂句。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Not one place, two meanings, an era, and a festival
culture_cards.title_zh: 不是一個地方、兩個意思、一個時代，和一個音樂節
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about jazz and swing.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於爵士樂與搖擺的四個小故事。

cards.en: Not one place, not one day
cards.zh: 不是一個地方、一個日子
cards.body_en: Jazz is said to have originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. But the Jazz article also says it did not begin as a single musical tradition in New Orleans or elsewhere. A single birthday for jazz is a convenient story, not a fact.
cards.body_zh: 一般說爵士樂是十九世紀末到二十世紀初，從紐奧良的非裔美國人社群發展出來的。但同一篇條目也說，它並不是從紐奧良或別處的某一個傳統開始的。給爵士樂一個生日，是方便的故事，不是事實。

cards.body_en: The word swing has two main uses in music. One is the technique we heard: lengthening and shortening the notes in each pair. The other is a style of jazz, “swing music”, that developed in the United States in the late 1920s and early 1930s and was dominant from 1935 to 1946. Taiwan’s dictionary describes 搖擺樂 as emphasizing the weak beats of the bar.
cards.body_zh: 「swing」在音樂裡有兩個主要用法。一個是我們聽到的技巧：把每一對音的前一個拉長、後一個縮短。另一個是一種爵士樂的風格「搖擺樂」，在 1920 年代末到 1930 年代初的美國形成，1935 到 1946 年最盛行。台灣的辭典描述搖擺樂強調小節裡的下半拍或弱拍。

cards.body_en: The rhythm section, piano, bass, and drums, provides the underlying rhythm, harmony, and pulse. The core elements are usually the drum kit and bass. In a swing band, the classic rhythm section was a quartet of electric guitar, piano, double bass, and drums. As bebop evolved, smaller groups dropped the guitar.
cards.body_zh: 節奏組，鋼琴、貝斯和鼓，提供底下的節奏、和聲與脈動。核心通常是鼓組和貝斯。搖擺樂團的經典節奏組是電吉他、鋼琴、低音提琴和鼓的四重奏。隨著咆勃（bebop）發展，較小的團體把吉他拿掉了。

cards.body_en: The Taichung Jazz Festival is an annual jazz music festival held in the West District of Taichung. According to Wikipedia, it started in 2003 and is held in October. We could not find a source for other facts about jazz in Taiwan, so we leave them out.
cards.body_zh: 台中爵士音樂節是每年在台中西區舉行的爵士音樂節。依 Wikipedia，它從 2003 年開始，在十月舉行。關於台灣爵士樂的其他事，我們查不到可靠的出處，所以不寫。

myths.myth_en: Jazz was born in one place on one date.
myths.myth_zh: 爵士樂在一個地方、一個日子誕生。
myths.fact_en: It grew out of African-American communities in New Orleans, but it did not begin as a single tradition in one place.
myths.fact_zh: 它從紐奧良的非裔美國人社群發展出來，但並不是在一個地方、從一個傳統開始的。

myths.myth_en: Jazz is all improvised, and so it is random.
myths.myth_zh: 爵士樂全是即興，所以是亂彈。
myths.fact_en: Improvisation is usually done over a chord progression. Swing-era big bands relied more on arrangements that were written or memorized.
myths.fact_zh: 即興通常是在和弦進行上做的。搖擺時代的大樂團比較倚賴寫好或背熟的編曲。

myths.myth_en: Swing is exactly a 2:1 triplet feel.
myths.myth_zh: 搖擺剛好就是 2:1 的三連音。
myths.fact_en: 2:1 is how swing is often understood. In practice the ratio is often more subtle, typically between 1:1 and 3:1, and it varies.
myths.fact_zh: 2:1 是人們常用來理解搖擺的方式。實際上比例常常細微得多，通常在 1:1 到 3:1 之間，而且會變。

myths.myth_en: Jazz standards were all written by jazz composers.
myths.myth_zh: 爵士標準曲都是爵士作曲家寫的。
myths.fact_en: Not all jazz standards were written by jazz composers.
myths.fact_zh: 不是所有爵士標準曲都是爵士作曲家寫的。

tricks.body_en: The first eighth note is lengthened, the second shortened.
tricks.body_zh: 前面的八分音符拉長，後面的縮短。

tricks.body_en: Only the off-beat notes move.
tricks.body_zh: 只有反拍的音在動。

tricks.body_en: Typically between 1:1 and 3:1, wider when slow.
tricks.body_zh: 通常在 1:1 到 3:1 之間，慢的時候比較大。

tricks.body_en: The chord progression guides the notes.
tricks.body_zh: 和弦進行指引著音。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The hi-hat is a bright, high sound, so it can feel sharper than it is loud.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。hi-hat 是明亮的高音，會比它的音量讓人覺得更尖。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: At a live concert, stand away from the speakers, and give your ears a quiet break afterward.
safety.zh: 在現場音樂會，離喇叭遠一點，結束後讓耳朵安靜休息一下。

materials.en: A short, familiar rhyme or nursery song
materials.zh: 一首短短的、大家熟悉的童謠

materials.en: Your hands for clapping
materials.zh: 用來拍手的雙手

steps.en: Clap a steady beat, four counts, and keep it going all the time.
steps.zh: 拍一個穩定的拍子，數四拍，一直保持。

steps.en: Say the rhyme with two equal syllables on each beat: “ti-ti, ti-ti”.
steps.zh: 把童謠念出來，每一拍兩個一樣長的音節：「ti-ti, ti-ti」。

steps.en: Say it again, but make the first syllable longer and the second shorter: “long-short, long-short”. Do not change the clapping.
steps.zh: 再念一次，但把前面的音節拉長、後面的縮短：「長—短，長—短」。拍手不要改。

steps.en: Talk about it: what changed, and what stayed the same?
steps.zh: 討論：什麼變了？什麼沒變？

activities.tip_en: The beat stays the same; only the words move. If the clapping speeds up, start again.
activities.tip_zh: 拍子不變，只有字在動。如果拍手跟著變快，就重來。

materials.en: A desk or drum for the “bass drum”
materials.zh: 一張桌子或鼓，當作「低音鼓」

materials.en: Classroom percussion, such as a tambourine or blocks
materials.zh: 教室打擊樂器，例如鈴鼓或木塊

materials.en: One singer or player as the soloist
materials.zh: 一位歌者或演奏者當獨奏者

steps.en: One group plays steady quarter notes, like a walking bass: one note on every beat.
steps.zh: 一組彈穩定的四分音符，像行走低音：每一拍一個音。

steps.en: A second group plays only on beats 2 and 4.
steps.zh: 第二組只在第二拍和第四拍敲。

steps.en: The soloist invents a short phrase over it, and the group answers: call and response.
steps.zh: 獨奏者在上面創造一個短樂句，大家回答：呼應。

steps.en: Swap roles and try again.
steps.zh: 換角色，再來一次。

activities.tip_en: Let the soloist use only two or three notes at first. A small set of notes makes improvising easier.
activities.tip_zh: 一開始讓獨奏者只用兩、三個音。音少一點，即興比較容易。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The tune, bass line, and hi-hat are our own simple model, and their timing is covered by automatic tests.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的名稱、年代與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；旋律、低音與 hi-hat 是我們自己的簡單模型，時間排列有自動測試。

sources.en: A music genre that originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans in the late 19th and early 20th centuries; jazz did not begin as a single musical tradition in New Orleans or elsewhere; characterized by swing and blue notes, complex chords, call and response vocals, polyrhythms and improvisation; difficult to define; big bands relied more on arrangements; free jazz explored playing without regular meter, beat
sources.zh: 十九世紀末到二十世紀初在紐奧良非裔美國人社群中形成的音樂類型；爵士樂並非從紐奧良或別處的單一傳統開始；特色是搖擺與藍調音、複雜和弦、呼應、多重節奏與即興；很難定義；大樂團比較倚賴編曲；自由爵士探索沒有規則拍子與節拍的演奏

sources.en: In swing rhythm the pulse is divided unequally; first note of each pair often understood to be twice as long as the second, implying a triplet feel; in practice the ratio is less definitive and often much more subtle; typically between 1:1 and 3:1, and can vary considerably; wider at slower tempos and narrower at faster tempos; swing is typically applied to eighth notes
sources.zh: 在搖擺節奏裡脈動被不平均地切開；每對音的第一個常被理解成第二個的兩倍長（三連音的感覺）；實際上比例常常更不確定、更細微；通常在 1:1 到 3:1 之間，變化很大；速度慢時較寬、速度快時較窄；搖擺通常用在八分音符上

sources.en: A style of jazz that developed in the United States during the late 1920s and early 1930s; from 1935 to 1946, known as the swing era; swing bands usually featured soloists who would improvise over the arrangement
sources.zh: 一種爵士樂風格，1920 年代末到 1930 年代初形成於美國；1935 到 1946 年稱為搖擺時代；搖擺樂團通常有獨奏者在編曲上即興

sources.en: The spontaneous invention of melodic solo lines or accompaniment parts in a performance of jazz music; inventing melodies and lines over a chord progression; rhythm section members typically improvise their accompaniment parts, an activity called comping
sources.zh: 在爵士演出中當場創造旋律獨奏線條或伴奏聲部；在和弦進行上創造旋律與線條；節奏組成員通常即興自己的伴奏，叫做 comping

sources.en: The standard rhythm section is piano, bass, and drums; a rhythm section provides the underlying rhythm, harmony and pulse; walking basslines generally consist of unsyncopated notes of equal value, usually quarter notes; in swing bands the classic rhythm section is electric guitar, piano, double bass and drums; bebop groups dropped the guitar
sources.zh: 標準節奏組是鋼琴、貝斯、鼓；節奏組提供底下的節奏、和聲與脈動；行走低音通常是沒有切分、音值相等的音，通常是四分音符；搖擺樂團的經典節奏組是電吉他、鋼琴、低音提琴與鼓；咆勃的小團體把吉他拿掉

sources.en: A blue note is a note sung or played at a slightly different pitch from standard, typically between a quartertone and a semitone; call and response is a succession of two distinct phrases that works like a conversation in music; syncopation is a placement of rhythmic stresses where they would not normally occur
sources.zh: 藍調音是用和標準音高稍微不同的音高唱或奏的音，通常相差四分之一音到半音；呼應是兩個不同樂句相連，像音樂裡的對話；切分音是把節奏重音放在平常不會出現的地方

sources.en: Twelve-bar blues is predominantly based on the I, IV, and V chords of a key; not all jazz standards were written by jazz composers
sources.zh: 十二小節藍調主要建立在一個調的 I、IV、V 和弦上；不是所有爵士標準曲都是爵士作曲家寫的

sources.en: Louis Armstrong (August 4, 1901 – July 6, 1971); Duke Ellington (April 29, 1899 – May 24, 1974), who said “It’s all music”; the Taichung Jazz Festival started in 2003 and is held annually in October
sources.zh: 路易斯・阿姆斯壯（1901 年 8 月 4 日–1971 年 7 月 6 日）；艾靈頓公爵（1899 年 4 月 29 日–1974 年 5 月 24 日），他說過「這全是音樂」；台中爵士音樂節從 2003 年開始，每年十月舉行
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Louis Armstrong”, “Duke Ellington” and “Taichung Jazz Festival”

sources.en: A music type that began in the United States; the music emphasizes the off beats or weak beats of the bar, which creates the feeling of swing; it is a main form of jazz pieces
sources.zh: 早期發源於美國的一種音樂類型……音樂強調小節裡的下半拍或弱拍，因而帶來搖擺的感覺。是爵士樂曲中的主要音樂形式。
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「搖擺樂」

sources.en: Syncopation: by tying the same notes, the strong and weak beats are shifted. Improvisation: arising from the interest of the moment. Blues: slow jazz music and songs with a hint of melancholy, from the American South at the end of the 19th century
sources.zh: 切分音：樂理規則中，經由同音的結合，使強弱拍子異動，稱為切分音。即興：隨當時的興致所生。藍調：源於十九世紀末美國南部，慢速含有幾許憂鬱氣氛的爵士音樂、歌曲。
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「即興」「切分音」「藍調」

sources.en: swing 搖擺樂：爵士樂的一個特定風格，始於 1935 年左右；jazz 爵士音樂；improvisation 即興演奏（唱）；syncopation 切分法；切分音；blue note 藍調音
sources.zh: swing: a specific style of jazz, beginning around 1935; jazz; improvisation; syncopation; blue note

lessons.title: What Music Grew in Taiwan?
lessons.title_zh: 台灣這塊土地上有哪些音樂？
lessons.blurb_en: Four ways to layer voices, heard with our own tune, and what people in Taiwan say about their own singing: indigenous peoples, Hakka, Hokkien, Nanguan, and Beiguan.
lessons.blurb_zh: 用我們自己的旋律聽四種疊聲部的方式，再讀台灣各個族群怎麼說自己的歌：原住民族、客家、閩南、南管與北管。
lessons.big_idea_en: Voices can be layered in different ways: all together, one after another, over a held note, or moving in parallel. People in Taiwan sing in all of these ways, and some songs belong to a time and a place, so we describe them and we do not copy them.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 聲部可以用不同的方式疊起來：一起唱、一個接一個、在拉長的音上、或平行移動。台灣各地的人用這些方式唱歌，有些歌屬於特定的時間與場合，所以我們描述它們，不複製它們。

lab.how_en: We wrote one short tune of 16 beats. Choose a way of layering and a number of voices, then press play. Each voice has its own color on the piano roll. The tune and all four ways are our own simple model. They are not songs of any people or tradition, and they are not recordings.
lab.how_zh: 我們寫了一段 16 拍的短旋律。選一種疊法和聲部數，再按播放。鋼琴卷上每個聲部有自己的顏色。旋律和四種疊法都是我們自己的簡單模型，不是任何族群或樂種的歌，也不是錄音。

paras: Many kinds of music grew in Taiwan, and people sing them in different languages. Taiwanese folk songs can be sorted by ethnic group and language: songs of the indigenous peoples in their own languages, Hakka folk songs mainly in Hakka, and Hokkien folk songs mainly in Taiwanese Hokkien. The Council of Indigenous Peoples recognizes 16 indigenous peoples officially. In this lesson we ask one question about all of them: how can voices be layered?

There are some useful words. In unison, two or more parts sound the same pitch, or pitches an octave apart. In a round, each voice sings the same melody, but each begins at a different time. A drone is a note or chord that is sounded continuously throughout most or all of a piece. Polyphony is a texture of two or more simultaneous lines of independent melody. Heterophony is the simultaneous variation of a single melodic line.

Several indigenous peoples of Taiwan are known for polyphonic singing. The Amis, Bunun, Paiwan, Rukai, and Tsou are known for their polyphonic vocals, and each has a unique variety. The Council of Indigenous Peoples says Amis songs use lead-and-answer singing, chanting, and polyphonic counterpoint. The Bunun style called eight-part harmony starts with four parts, and the “eight” comes from overtones that appear at a high register. It is sung on vowels, without words.

Some songs belong to a time and a place. According to Chinese Wikipedia, Amis ritual music is mostly sung only at specific ceremonies. The Council of Indigenous Peoples says the sacred ancestral songs of the Thao are not to be sung casually. Taiwan’s 2007 Act for the protection of indigenous traditional intellectual creations lists music and songs, and a right holder may license their use. That is why this lesson describes the ways of singing, and does not copy any song.

Han traditions layer sound in other ways. Nanguan is an old kind of music popular in Fujian, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia. The singer holds clappers, and the accompaniment is led by the pipa, with the xiao, sanxian, erxian, and a set of four boards. It is described as typically slow and gentle, and as heterophonic. Beiguan is another Han tradition in Taiwan; its name is paired with Nanguan, and “north” also stands for a lively, high-pitched style.

Hakka mountain songs are short in form with free rhythm, and are popular in mountain villages. The main tunes are the old mountain song, the mountain-song-zi, and the pingban. The tunes are fixed, and the words can be changed and improvised. Shange has traditionally been sung while people work, particularly while picking tea. Taiwanese opera developed in Taiwan after folk arts came from southern Fujian, and its tunes were taken from folk songs.
paras_zh: 台灣長出了許多種音樂，人們用不同的語言唱。台灣民謠可以依族群與語言分類：原住民族用自己語言唱的歌、主要用客語的客家民謠，和主要用台灣閩南語的閩南語民謠。原住民族委員會官方認定的原住民族有 16 族。這一課對它們問同一個問題：聲部可以怎麼疊？
有幾個有用的詞。齊唱（unison）是兩個以上的聲部唱同一個音高，或相差八度的音高。輪唱（round）是每個聲部唱同一條旋律，但各自在不同的時間開始。持續音（drone）是在一首曲子的大部分或全部時間裡，持續發聲的一個音或和弦。複音（polyphony）是兩條或以上同時進行、各自獨立的旋律線所形成的織度。異音（heterophony）是同一條旋律線同時出現變化。
台灣有好幾個原住民族以複音歌唱聞名。阿美族、布農族、排灣族、魯凱族和鄒族以複音的人聲聞名，而且各有獨特的類型。原住民族委員會說，阿美族的歌謠有領唱與答唱、吟唱，以及複音對位。布農族稱為八部合音的唱法，開始時只有四部，「八」來自高音域出現的泛音。它用母音來唱，沒有歌詞。
有些歌屬於特定的時間與場合。依中文維基百科，阿美族的祭儀音樂多半只在特定儀式的特定場合吟唱。原住民族委員會說，邵族的祖靈祭歌謠具有神聖性，平日禁止隨意吟唱。台灣 2007 年的《原住民族傳統智慧創作保護條例》把音樂與歌曲列入，權利人也可以授權他人使用。所以這一課只描述唱法，不複製任何一首歌。
漢人的傳統用別的方式疊聲音。南管是流行於福建、台灣與東南亞的古樂。歌者拿拍板，伴奏以琵琶為主，再配洞簫、三弦、二弦、四塊板。它被描述為通常緩慢、柔和，並且是異音的。北管是台灣另一種漢人傳統，名稱與南管相對，「北」也用來表示熱鬧高亢的風格。
客家山歌形式短小、節奏自由，流行於山村。主要的調子是老山歌、山歌子和平板。曲調固定，歌詞可以變化、即興。山歌傳統上在工作時唱，特別是採茶的時候。歌仔戲是閩南的民間藝術傳到台灣後發展出來的，曲調採自歌謠小調。
questions: What is the difference between a unison and a round?
Is the Bunun “eight-part” style really eight parts?
Why does this lesson not play real songs?
answers: In unison, voices sing the same pitch at the same time. In a round, each voice sings the same melody but begins at a different time.
It starts with four parts, and the “eight” comes from overtones at a high register.
Some songs are sung only at the right time and place, and the music of recognized works can be licensed, so we describe how people sing and do not copy their songs.

vocab.exzh: 全班齊唱。

vocab.ex: In a round, each group starts later.
vocab.exzh: 輪唱時，每一組晚一點開始。

vocab.ex: A drone is a held low note.
vocab.exzh: 持續音是一個拉長的低音。

vocab.ex: Polyphony has several independent melodies.
vocab.exzh: 複音有好幾條各自獨立的旋律。

vocab.ex: The chorus has four parts.
vocab.exzh: 這個合唱團有四個聲部。

vocab.ex: A folk song is passed on by people.
vocab.exzh: 民謠由民間代代傳下來。

vocab.ex: A ritual song belongs to a ceremony.
vocab.exzh: 祭儀歌曲屬於一個儀式。

vocab.ex: A nanguan ensemble has five instruments.
vocab.exzh: 南管的合奏團通常有五件樂器。

quiz.q: In a round, what do the voices do?
options: Sing the same melody, each beginning at a different time

quiz.q: What is a drone?
options: A note or chord sounded continuously through most of a piece

quiz.q: How many peoples does the Council of Indigenous Peoples officially recognize?
What does the Bunun eight-part style start with?
Why does this lesson describe ways of singing instead of playing real songs?
options: Some songs belong to a time and place, and recognized works can be licensed
Because real songs are too short
Because the computer cannot play them

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It · 動手試試

parts.text_en: Three voices sing exactly the same pitches. The sound gets thicker, but the notes do not change.
parts.text_zh: 三個聲部唱完全一樣的音高。聲音變厚，但音沒有不同。

parts.text_en: Each voice comes in four beats after the one before. Watch the colors step to the right.
parts.text_zh: 每個聲部比前一個晚四拍進來。看顏色一階一階往右。

parts.text_en: One voice sings the tune. The others hold a long low C underneath all the way through.
parts.text_zh: 一個聲部唱旋律，其他聲部在底下一直拉長一個低音 C。

parts.text_en: The other voices move with the tune on different notes of the scale.
parts.text_zh: 其他聲部在音階裡的不同音上，跟著旋律走。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the game below: can you tell which way of layering it is?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試下面的遊戲：你分得出是哪一種疊法嗎？

layerq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays our tune with two to four voices. Choose the way of layering. If you cannot hear the sound, press “What is in the music”.
layerq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題用兩到四個聲部播放我們的旋律。選出疊法。如果聽不到聲音，按「音樂裡有什麼」。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The curriculum names unison, round, and chorus singing, Taiwanese songs, and local and traditional music. It does not name Hakka, Nanguan, Beiguan, or any indigenous people in its music items.
curric.lead_zh: 課綱寫到齊唱、輪唱與合唱、臺灣歌謠，以及本土與傳統音樂。音樂項目裡沒有出現客家、南管、北管，也沒有任何一個原住民族的名字。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 多元形式歌曲，如：獨唱、齊唱等。基礎歌唱技巧，如：聲音探索、姿勢等。
items.note_en: Singing alone and singing in unison.
items.note_zh: 獨唱與齊唱。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 多元形式歌曲，如：輪唱、合唱等。基礎歌唱技巧，如：呼吸、共鳴等。
items.note_en: Round and chorus singing are named here.
items.note_zh: 這裡寫到輪唱與合唱。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 器樂曲與聲樂曲，如：獨奏曲、臺灣歌謠、藝術歌曲，以及樂曲之創作背景或歌詞內涵。
items.note_en: Taiwanese songs, and the background of a song.
items.note_zh: 臺灣歌謠，與歌曲的創作背景。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 器樂曲與聲樂曲，如：各國民謠、本土與傳統音樂、古典與流行音樂等，以及樂曲之作曲家、演奏者、傳統藝師與創作背景。
items.note_en: Local and traditional music, and traditional artists.
items.note_zh: 本土與傳統音樂，與傳統藝師。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Sixteen peoples, a right time, four parts or eight, and tunes that stay while words change
culture_cards.title_zh: 十六族、對的時間、四部還是八部、曲調不變而歌詞會變
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories. We describe; we do not copy.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事。我們描述，不複製。

cards.body_en: The Council of Indigenous Peoples lists 16 peoples: Amis, Atayal, Paiwan, Bunun, Puyuma, Rukai, Tsou, Saisiyat, Tao (Yami), Thao, Kavalan, Truku, Sakizaya, Seediq, Hla’alua, and Kanakanavu. Some scholars say these 16 groupings do not reflect social entities and are administrative categories. Each people has its own languages, songs, and customs.
cards.body_zh: 原住民族委員會列出 16 族：阿美、泰雅、排灣、布農、卑南、魯凱、鄒、賽夏、雅美（達悟）、邵、噶瑪蘭、太魯閣、撒奇萊雅、賽德克、拉阿魯哇、卡那卡那富。有學者說這 16 個分類並不反映社會實體，是行政上的分類。每一族有自己的語言、歌與習俗。

cards.body_en: Amis ritual music is mostly sung only at the specific ceremonies. The Thao sacred ancestral songs are not sung casually. Under the 2007 Act, music and songs are named among traditional creations; only works that are recognized and registered receive protection, and a right holder may license use. Education use of published works is allowed, with the source stated.
cards.body_zh: 阿美族的祭儀音樂多半只在特定儀式的特定場合吟唱。邵族的祖靈祭歌謠不隨意吟唱。依 2007 年的條例，音樂與歌曲列在傳統智慧創作裡；只有經認定並登記的才受保護，權利人可授權他人使用。已發表的創作為教育而使用是允許的，並要註明出處。

cards.k: Four or Eight · 四部還是八部
cards.en: Four parts, eight voices of sound
cards.body_en: The Bunun eight-part style is often named that way, but it is not eight parts in the vocal sense. It starts with four parts, and overtones make it sound like eight. The number of singers is also not eight: Chinese Wikipedia says it can go up to twelve people. Only two Bunun subgroups sing it, so not all Bunun do.
cards.body_zh: 布農族的八部合音常被這樣稱呼，但並不是聲樂中的八部。它從四部開始，因為出現泛音而聽起來像八部。歌者的人數也不是八個：中文維基百科說可以增加到十二人。只有布農族的兩個群體唱它，所以不是所有布農人都唱。

cards.k: Fixed Tune, New Words · 曲調固定、歌詞變
cards.body_en: Hakka mountain songs have three main tunes: the old mountain song, the mountain-song-zi, and the pingban. The tunes are fixed, and the words can be changed freely and improvised. Pingban is also called the “improved tune”. Chinese Wikipedia notes the figure “nine accents and eighteen tunes” is generally taken as a figure of speech, not an exact count.
cards.body_zh: 客家山歌有三大調：老山歌、山歌子和平板。曲調固定，歌詞可以隨意變化、即興創作。平板又稱「改良調」。中文維基百科說，「九腔十八調」一般認為是虛詞，不是精確的數字。

myths.myth_en: The Bunun eight-part style has eight vocal parts.
myths.myth_zh: 布農族的八部合音有八個聲部。
myths.fact_en: It starts with four parts. Overtones at a high register make it sound like eight.
myths.fact_zh: 它從四部開始。高音域出現的泛音，讓它聽起來像八部。

myths.myth_en: Songs of Taiwan’s indigenous peoples are free for anyone to record and reuse.
myths.myth_zh: 原住民族的歌誰都可以隨意錄音、重複使用。
myths.fact_en: Some songs are sung only at the proper occasion. Recognized, registered works are protected, and a right holder may license their use.
myths.fact_zh: 有些歌只在適當的場合唱。經認定並登記的創作受保護，權利人可以授權他人使用。

myths.myth_en: All indigenous peoples in Taiwan sing the same way.
myths.myth_zh: 台灣所有原住民族都用同一種方式唱歌。
myths.fact_en: Each has its own variety. For example, the eight-part style is sung by only two Bunun subgroups.
myths.fact_zh: 各族有自己的類型。例如八部合音只有布農族的兩個群體唱。

myths.myth_en: “Harvest festival” is the name every Amis community uses.
myths.myth_zh: 「豐年祭」是所有阿美族部落自己的名稱。
myths.fact_en: Chinese Wikipedia says the local names do not carry the meaning of harvest, and that the term was given from outside.
myths.fact_zh: 中文維基百科說，各地的稱呼幾乎都不帶有「豐收」的意思，這個名稱是外來的。

tricks.body_en: Same pitch at the same time.
tricks.body_zh: 同一個音高，同一個時刻。

tricks.body_en: Same tune, each voice enters later.
tricks.body_zh: 同一條旋律，每個聲部晚一點進來。

tricks.body_en: One note held through the tune.
tricks.body_zh: 一個音從頭拉到尾。

tricks.body_en: Some songs belong to a time and place.
tricks.body_zh: 有些歌屬於特定的時間與場合。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears and Voice · 保護耳朵與聲音

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. Four voices together are louder than one, even with our mixing.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。四個聲部在一起，即使經過我們的混音，還是比一個聲部大聲。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: When you sing along, stay in a comfortable range. If your throat hurts, stop and drink some water.
safety.zh: 跟著唱的時候，留在舒服的音域。如果喉嚨痛，就停下來喝點水。

activities.title_en: Four Ways to Sing One Song

materials.en: A short song or rhyme your class already knows (not a ceremonial song)
materials.zh: 一首全班已經會的短歌或童謠（不是祭儀歌曲）

materials.en: A space where groups can stand apart
materials.zh: 可以讓各組分開站的空間

steps.en: Everyone sings it together: unison.
steps.zh: 全班一起唱：齊唱。

steps.en: Divide into three groups. Group 1 begins; Group 2 enters when Group 1 finishes the first line; Group 3 enters after Group 2: a round.
steps.zh: 分成三組。第一組開始；第一組唱完第一句，第二組進來；第二組之後，第三組進來：輪唱。

steps.en: A few singers hum one low note all the way through while the rest sing: a drone.
steps.zh: 幾位歌者從頭到尾哼一個低音，其他人唱歌：持續音。

steps.en: Let one group sing the same rhythm a little higher or lower, if they can find it: parts.
steps.zh: 讓一組用同樣的節奏唱得稍高或稍低（找得到的話）：分部。

steps.en: Talk about it: which sounded thickest? Which was easiest to follow?
steps.zh: 討論：哪一種聽起來最厚？哪一種最容易跟著唱？

activities.tip_en: Choose a song with a clear, steady beat. A round needs a tune that can be sung one after another.
activities.tip_zh: 選節拍清楚穩定的歌。輪唱需要可以一個接一個唱下去的旋律。

materials.en: A family member, teacher, or community member who is willing to talk
materials.zh: 一位願意聊聊的家人、老師或社區裡的人

materials.en: Paper and a pen
materials.zh: 紙和筆

steps.en: Ask: what songs does your family or community sing? When are they sung?
steps.zh: 問：你的家人或社區唱哪些歌？什麼時候唱？

steps.en: Ask: are there songs that are only for certain times or places?
steps.zh: 問：有沒有只在特定時間或地點唱的歌？

steps.en: Ask: how would you like others to learn about them?
steps.zh: 問：你希望別人怎麼認識它們？

steps.en: Write down what you learned, and do not record or share it without asking.
steps.zh: 把學到的寫下來；沒有問過，不錄音也不分享。

activities.tip_en: Listening comes first. Say thank you, and give the person’s name and community when you share what they told you, if they agree.
activities.tip_zh: 先聽。說謝謝；對方同意的話，分享時註明是誰、哪個社區說的。

links_head.zh: 這一課的前面、旁邊和後面

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The tune and the four ways of layering are our own simple model; no song of any people or tradition is reproduced.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的名稱、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；旋律與四種疊法是我們自己的簡單模型，沒有複製任何族群或樂種的歌。

sources.en: The Amis, Bunun, Paiwan, Rukai and Tsou are known for their polyphonic vocals, of which each has a unique variety; Shan'ge has traditionally been sung while people work, particularly during tea picking; Holo folk music
sources.zh: 阿美、布農、排灣、魯凱、鄒以複音人聲聞名，各有獨特的類型；山歌傳統上在工作時唱，特別是採茶；福佬民謠

sources.en: The Council of Indigenous Peoples grants recognized status; some scholars hold that these 16 groupings do not reflect any social entities
sources.zh: 原住民族委員會給予認定；有學者認為這 16 個分類並不反映任何社會實體
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Taiwanese indigenous peoples” and “Council of Indigenous Peoples”

sources.en: The list of the 16 peoples: 阿美族、泰雅族、排灣族、布農族、卑南族、魯凱族、鄒族、賽夏族、雅美族、邵族、噶瑪蘭族、太魯閣族、撒奇萊雅族、賽德克族、拉阿魯哇族、卡那卡那富族
sources.zh: 十六族名單：阿美族、泰雅族、排灣族、布農族、卑南族、魯凱族、鄒族、賽夏族、雅美族、邵族、噶瑪蘭族、太魯閣族、撒奇萊雅族、賽德克族、拉阿魯哇族、卡那卡那富族
sources.src: 原住民族委員會「原住民族16族簡介」

sources.en: Songs use lead-and-answer singing, chanting, and polyphonic counterpoint, showing the different needs of religious ritual, banquets, and leisure
sources.zh: 歌謠用領唱與答唱、吟唱歌詠及複音對位的方式，呈現宗教儀式、宴會交誼與休閒需求的不同表現
sources.src: 原住民族委員會「阿美族」

sources.en: The song actually starts with only four parts; when the range goes up to a certain level, eight different pitches appear on the sound track, so people call it eight-part harmony
sources.zh: 歌曲一開始，其實只有四部合音，但當音域高到某個層次時，音軌會出現八個不同的音階，因此被世人稱之為八部合音
sources.src: 原住民族委員會「布農族」

sources.en: Ancestral-spirit ritual songs are sacred, and may not be sung casually on ordinary days
sources.zh: 祖靈祭歌謠具有神聖性，平日禁止隨意吟唱。

sources.en: Often called eight-part, but not eight parts in vocal music; it is a four-part chorus that sounds like eight because of overtones; up to twelve people; sung on meaningless vowels; only among the Bunun Luan and Jun groups; Amis ritual music is sung only at specific ceremonies; the name for the harvest festival rarely carries the meaning of harvest
sources.zh: 常被稱為八部合音，但並非聲樂中的八部，而是四部合唱曲，因為出現泛音而聽起來像是有八部；可增加至十二人；歌詞全以無意義之母音來演唱；僅流傳於布農族巒社群和郡社群；阿美族祭儀音樂多半只在特定儀式舉行時吟唱；「豐年祭」多不帶有「豐收」之意涵
sources.src: 中文維基百科「八部合音」「阿美族」

sources.en: Art. 3: traditional ritual, music, dance, songs ...; Art. 4: only works that are recognized and registered are protected; Art. 13: the right holder may license use; Art. 16: use needed for reporting, commentary, education or research must state the source
sources.zh: 第 3 條：傳統之宗教祭儀、音樂、舞蹈、歌曲……；第 4 條：應經主管機關認定並登記，始受保護；第 13 條：專用權人得授權他人使用；第 16 條：為報導、評論、教育或研究之必要使用，應註明出處
sources.src: 全國法規資料庫《原住民族傳統智慧創作保護條例》

sources.en: Old music popular in Fujian, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia since the Song and Yuan; the singer holds clappers, and the accompaniment is mainly pipa with dongxiao, sanxian, erxian, and four boards
sources.zh: 宋元以後，流行於福建、臺灣及東南亞地區的古樂……歌者執拍板，伴奏樂器以琵琶為主，再配以洞簫、三弦、二弦、四塊板等樂器。
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「南管」

sources.en: Nanguan is typically slow, gentle, delicate and melodic, heterophonic; 北管為臺灣漢族傳統音樂的其中一種……「北」也用來表示較熱鬧高亢的音樂風格
sources.zh: 南管通常緩慢、柔和、細緻而有旋律性，是異音的；北管是台灣漢族傳統音樂的一種，「北」也表示較熱鬧高亢的風格
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Nanguan music” and 中文維基百科「北管」

sources.en: Mountain song: a short, free-rhythm folk song popular in mountain villages. Taiwanese opera: folk arts from southern Fujian came to Taiwan and gradually developed into an independent genre. Folk song: simple music passed down among the people
sources.zh: 山歌：一種形式短小，節奏自由，曲調爽朗質樸，流行於山村間的民歌。歌仔戲：明末閩南的錦歌、採茶曲、車鼓弄等民間藝術傳入臺灣後……逐漸發展成為獨立戲種。民謠：民間歌謠，由民間流傳下來的純樸音樂
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「山歌」「歌仔戲」「民謠」

sources.en: Mountain songs have wide content and simple form, and the words are improvised; the old mountain song, mountain-song-zi, and pingban are the three main tunes; pingban is also called the “improved tune”
sources.zh: 「山歌」演唱的內容廣泛，曲式結構簡單，歌詞具有即興特點；把「老山歌」、「山歌子」、「平板」歸為三大調；「平板」……故又稱為「改良調」
sources.src: 教育部《客家語辭典》「客家山歌」（鄭榮興）

sources.en: The three tunes are fixed, and the words can be changed and improvised; “nine accents and eighteen tunes” is generally taken as a figure of speech; Taiwanese folk songs are sorted into indigenous, Hakka, and Taiwanese Hokkien; Taiwanese opera tunes are taken from folk ballads
sources.zh: 此三調之曲調固定，歌詞可隨意變化、即興創作；一般認為「九腔十八調」為虛詞；台灣民謠可依種族與語言分為原住民族、客家民謠與臺灣閩南話民謠；歌仔戲曲調採自歌謠小調
sources.src: 中文維基百科「客家山歌」「台灣民謠」「歌仔戲」

sources.en: Unison: parts that sound the same pitch or pitches an octave apart; round: multiple voices sing exactly the same melody, each beginning at different times; drone: a note or chord continuously sounded; polyphony: two or more simultaneous lines of independent melody; heterophony: simultaneous variation of a single melodic line
sources.zh: 齊唱：同一個音高或相差八度；輪唱：多個聲部唱同一旋律、各自在不同時間開始；持續音：持續發聲的一個音或和弦；複音：兩條以上同時進行、各自獨立的旋律線；異音：同一旋律線同時出現變化

sources.en: Round: a chorus is divided into two or more groups, each singing the same melody one after another at a set interval. Unison singing: two or more singers sing the same melody at the same time without parts. Chorus: many people divided into parts singing a multi-part tune together
sources.zh: 輪唱：一個合唱團將團員分成二組以上，每組按一定時距先後演唱同一旋律的歌曲。齊唱：兩位以上的歌唱者，不分聲部按照同一旋律同時演唱。合唱：將多數人分成幾個聲部，同時演唱多聲部的曲調
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「輪唱」「齊唱」「合唱」

sources.en: Taiwan's 12-year curriculum: arts (music) 音 E-Ⅱ-1, 音 E-Ⅲ-1, 音 A-Ⅱ-1, 音 A-Ⅲ-1

lessons.title: What Is Buddhist Chanting?
lessons.blurb_en: A long note, a breath, and a steady knock: hear how a group can sound together, and learn what the dictionary says about the instruments. Sound and rhythm only.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一個長音、一口氣、一下穩定的敲擊：聽一群人怎麼一起發聲，也讀讀辭典怎麼說這些樂器。只講聲音與節奏。
lessons.big_idea_en: A group can sound together by sharing one steady beat and by taking breaths at the right moments. This lesson is about sound and rhythm only.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 一群人可以靠一個穩定的拍子，和在對的時刻換氣，一起發出整齊的聲音。這一課只講聲音與節奏。

lab.how_en: We made a model with one long note, a short breath, and a wooden-fish-style knock on every beat. Choose how the voices breathe, together or in turn, and how many voices there are. Each lane is one voice: colored where it sings, empty where it breathes. This is our own model of sound. It is not a recording of any chanting, and it has no words or tune from any tradition.
lab.how_zh: 我們做了一個模型：一個長音、一口短短的氣，每一拍有一下木魚式的敲擊。選聲部怎麼換氣（一起或輪流）和聲部數。每一條是一個聲部：唱的時候有顏色，換氣的時候是空的。這是我們自己的聲音模型，不是任何唱誦的錄音，也沒有任何傳統的詞或曲調。

paras: In Chinese Buddhism, chanting is called fanbai. The Taiwan dictionary says it means, in China, chanting short verses or songs of praise. Chinese Wikipedia says it gradually took on a specific melody and rhythm to make reciting easier. The melodies are traditionally passed on by ear from one generation to the next, and the chanting book usually does not mark the melody. In this lesson we look only at the sound and the rhythm.

When a group chants, many people sing the same melody at the same time. In music this is called unison. Someone leads. The dictionary says the leader, the weina, starts the chant and leads the group by striking the small bell, the yinqing, in the morning and evening sessions. Those sessions are held every day, and everyone in the temple takes part.

A temple has many ritual instruments, called faqi. The dictionary lists instruments such as the fish, the cymbals, and the bell. The wooden fish has two shapes. One is a long, straight fish that hangs in a corridor, to call people to a meal or to gather them. The other is round, and it sits on a table when chanting. The round one is hollow, and the hollow sound changes with its size, material, and the hollow inside. Chinese Wikipedia says a bigger one has a lower pitch.

How is the wooden fish used? English Wikipedia says that in Chan, Seon, Zen, and Thien Buddhism, the wooden fish serves to maintain rhythm during chanting. The mallet often has a rubber-coated tip, which gives a muffled but clear sound. A wooden fish often rests on a cushion, to prevent unpleasant knocking sounds. That is why our model uses a short, quickly fading knock, once on every beat.

The small bell, the yinqing, is a small bowl-shaped copper bell with a wooden handle, used to get everyone’s attention. A bigger bowl-shaped bell, the qing, is struck during chanting and ceremonies. Be careful with the word qing. It also names an ancient hanging chime of stone or metal. The dictionary lists the two as different instruments that share a character.

How do many voices breathe? A singer cannot hold a note forever, so there must be breaths. If everyone breathes at the same time, there is a small gap in the sound. A technique for choirs, called staggered breathing, has each singer breathe at a different time, so that no breath gaps can be heard. We use it in our model to show the idea. We do not say that any chanting group does it. Chanting is not one sound either: it varies by tradition, with some more monotone and some more melodic.
paras_zh: 在漢傳佛教裡，唱誦叫做梵唄。台灣的辭典說，在中國，它指唱頌短偈或歌讚。中文維基百科說，它為了方便誦念，慢慢形成了特定的旋律與節奏。旋律傳統上是一代一代用耳朵傳下去的，課誦本通常也不標示旋律。這一課我們只看聲音與節奏。
一群人唱誦的時候，很多人同時唱同一條旋律。音樂上這叫齊唱（unison）。有人帶領。辭典說，帶領的維那在早晚課時起腔，並敲引磬領眾。這樣的早晚課每天都有，全寺的人一起參加。
寺院裡有很多法器。辭典列出的有魚、鐃、鈸、磬等。木魚有兩種形狀。一種是挺直的魚形，掛在走廊上，用來叫人吃飯或聚集大家。另一種是圓的，誦經時放在桌上。圓的是中空的，中空的聲音隨它的大小、材質和裡面的空腔而不同。中文維基百科說，木魚越大，音高越低。
木魚怎麼用？英文維基百科說，在禪宗（Chan、Seon、Zen、Thien）裡，木魚用來維持唱誦的節奏。木槌的前端常包著橡膠，敲出來悶悶的、但很清楚。木魚常放在軟墊上，避免敲出難聽的碰撞聲。所以我們的模型用短而快速消失的敲擊，每一拍一下。
引磬是小小的碗形銅鈴，附木柄，用來引起大家的注意。比較大的碗形的磬，則在誦經和法會時敲。要小心「磬」這個字。它也是古代用石頭或金屬做的懸掛樂器的名字。辭典把兩者列成不同的樂器，只是共用一個字。
很多人怎麼換氣？一個人不能一直拉著一個音，所以一定要換氣。如果大家同時換氣，聲音就會有一個小空隙。合唱團有一種技巧叫輪流換氣（staggered breathing），每個人在不同時間換氣，這樣就聽不到換氣的空隙。我們的模型用它來展示這個想法。我們並沒有說任何唱誦的團體這樣做。唱誦也不是只有一種聲音：因傳統而不同，有些比較接近單調，有些比較有旋律。
questions: What does the wooden fish do in a group chant?
What does a leader use the small bell for?
Why does our model use “breathe in turn”?
answers: English Wikipedia says that in Chan, Seon, Zen, and Thien Buddhism, it serves to maintain rhythm during chanting.
The dictionary says the leader strikes the small bell to start the chant and lead the group.
To show the choir technique of staggered breathing: no breath gaps can be heard. We do not claim that chanters use it.

vocab.ex: The group will chant together.
vocab.exzh: 大家會一起唱誦。

vocab.ex: They sang in unison.
vocab.exzh: 他們齊唱。

vocab.ex: The wooden fish is hollow.
vocab.exzh: 木魚是中空的。

vocab.ex: A small bell gets everyone’s attention.
vocab.exzh: 小小的鈴能引起大家的注意。

vocab.ex: A temple has many ritual instruments.
vocab.exzh: 寺院有很多法器。

vocab.ex: Take a breath before the long note.
vocab.exzh: 拉長音之前先吸一口氣。

vocab.ex: A steady beat does not speed up or slow down.
vocab.exzh: 穩定的拍子不會忽快忽慢。

vocab.ex: A hollow object makes a deeper sound.
vocab.exzh: 中空的東西會發出比較低沉的聲音。

quiz.q: What do many people singing the same melody at the same time call it?
According to the dictionary, what does the leader strike to lead the group?
What does the round wooden fish help to keep?
Why does staggered breathing make the sound continuous?
options: Each singer breathes at a different time

quiz.q: Which statement is true about the word qing (磬)?
options: It names only a stone chime
It names a kind of food

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It · 動手試試

parts.text_en: Six beats of singing, two beats of breath. The knocks keep going.
parts.text_zh: 唱六拍，換氣兩拍。敲擊繼續。

parts.text_en: The voices start and stop at the same time. The gap is the same size as for one voice.
parts.text_zh: 聲部同時開始、同時停。空隙和一個聲部時一樣大。

parts.text_en: Each voice breathes at a different time, so there is always a voice singing.
parts.text_zh: 每個聲部在不同的時間換氣，所以總有一個聲部在唱。

parts.text_en: More voices, each at a smaller volume. The knocks are still exactly on the beat.
parts.text_zh: 更多聲部，每個音量更小。敲擊還是剛好在拍子上。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the two games below: how long can you hold a note, and which knocks are steadier?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試下面兩個遊戲：你的一口氣能拉多長？哪一組的敲擊比較穩？

breath.lead_en: Press and hold the button to sing one note, and watch the bar. A real breath is short. Our model asks for six beats, about five seconds at a slow tempo.
breath.lead_zh: 按住按鈕唱一個長音，看進度條。真實的一口氣很短。我們的模型一次要六拍，在慢速度下約五秒。

steadyq.lead_en: Six questions. Listen to knock set A and knock set B. One keeps a steady beat, and the other wobbles a little. Choose the steady one. If you cannot hear the sound, press “What is in the knocks”.
steadyq.lead_zh: 六道題。聽 A 組和 B 組的敲擊。一組拍子穩定，另一組有點晃。選出穩定的那一組。如果聽不到聲音，按「敲擊裡有什麼」。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱

curric.lead_zh: 課綱寫到節奏、音樂與生活、音樂與群體活動，以及本土與傳統音樂。音樂項目裡沒有出現唱誦、法器或佛教這些詞。

items.text: 音樂元素，如：節奏、力度、速度等。
items.note_en: A steady beat and its speed.
items.note_zh: 穩定的拍子與它的速度。

items.text: 音樂與生活。
items.note_en: Music is part of daily life in many places.
items.note_zh: 音樂是許多地方日常生活的一部分。

items.note_en: Making sound together as a group.

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 器樂曲與聲樂曲，如：各國民謠、本土與傳統音樂、古典與流行音樂等，以及樂曲之作曲家、演奏者、傳統藝師與創作背景。
items.note_en: Local and traditional music.
items.note_zh: 本土與傳統音樂。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A word, two fish, two bells, and two styles
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個詞、兩種魚、兩種磬、兩種風格
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about sound and instruments. We leave the teachings to the teachers of each tradition.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於聲音與樂器的四個小故事。教義留給各傳統的老師來講。

cards.body_en: The dictionary describes fanbai as singing short verses or songs of praise. Chinese Wikipedia says the specific melodies came to be shaped to make reciting easier, and that the chanting book usually gives no melody marks. English Wikipedia says the melodies are traditionally passed on only by ear from generation to generation. Traditional accounts of where it began are contested, so we give no date.
cards.body_zh: 辭典把梵唄描述為唱頌短偈或歌讚。中文維基百科說，特定的旋律是為了方便誦念而形成的，課誦本通常不標示旋律。英文維基百科說，旋律傳統上只用耳朵一代傳一代。關於它從哪裡開始，傳統的說法有爭議，所以我們不寫年代。

cards.body_en: The dictionary says the wooden fish has two shapes. One is a long straight fish, hung in temple corridors to call people to a meal or to gather them. The other is a round fish, placed on a table when chanting. A different instrument, the fish drum, is a bamboo tube covered with fish skin, used in storytelling. It is not the temple wooden fish.
cards.body_zh: 辭典說木魚有兩種形狀。一種是挺直的魚形，掛在寺院走廊上，用來叫人吃飯或聚集大家。另一種是圓形的，誦經時放在桌上。另一件樂器魚鼓，是一端蒙魚皮的竹筒，用在說唱。它不是寺院的木魚。

cards.body_en: The dictionary lists two meanings for the character qing. One is an ancient hanging chime made of jade, stone, or metal, shaped like a carpenter’s square. The other is a hollow copper instrument shaped like a bowl, struck in temples. English Wikipedia’s article on standing bells adds that the word, which historically meant a lithophone used in state rituals, was more recently applied to this type of bell.
cards.body_zh: 辭典列出「磬」的兩個意思。一個是古代用玉石或金屬做的懸掛樂器，形狀像曲尺。另一個是寺院裡敲的碗形中空銅製樂器。英文維基百科的「站立式鈴」條目補充說，這個詞歷史上指國家儀式用的石磬，後來才被用在這一種鈴上。

cards.zh: 台灣聽得到的兩種風格
cards.body_en: Wikipedia says that in Taiwan, the styles of fanbai can mainly be divided into two types. The Gushan style is faster-paced, with more ornamentation around the core notes. The Haichaoyin style is slower, relaxed, and steady, with a simpler melody. Wikipedia does not cite a source for this, so we treat it as a second-hand description. We could not find an official record about fanbai.
cards.body_zh: 維基百科說，在台灣，梵唄的風格主要分成兩種。鼓山調速度較快，骨幹音上加花比較多。海潮音速度比較舒緩平穩，旋律比較簡單。維基百科沒有為這段話列出處，所以我們把它當作第二手的描述。我們也找不到關於梵唄的官方紀錄。

myths.myth_en: All Buddhist chanting sounds the same.
myths.myth_zh: 所有佛教的唱誦聽起來都一樣。
myths.fact_en: The intonation and style vary by tradition, some more monotone and others more melodic. Even in Taiwan, two styles are named.
myths.fact_zh: 音調與風格因傳統而不同，有的比較接近單調，有的比較有旋律。光在台灣，就有兩種風格。

myths.myth_en: The word “qing” always means a stone chime.
myths.myth_zh: 「磬」一定是石磬。
myths.fact_en: The dictionary lists two meanings: an ancient hanging chime, and a hollow copper bowl-shaped instrument struck in temples.
myths.fact_zh: 辭典列了兩個意思：古代的懸掛樂器，和寺院裡敲的碗形中空銅製樂器。

myths.myth_en: A wooden fish is a drum made from fish skin.
myths.myth_zh: 木魚是用魚皮做的鼓。
myths.fact_en: The wooden fish is a hollow wooden instrument. The fish drum, a different instrument, is covered with fish skin.
myths.fact_zh: 木魚是中空的木製樂器。魚鼓是另一種樂器，才蒙著魚皮。

myths.myth_en: Singing bowls are ancient chanting tools.
myths.myth_zh: 頌缽是古老的唱誦工具。
myths.fact_en: English Wikipedia says the manufacture and use of bowls specifically for “singing” is believed to be a modern phenomenon.
myths.fact_zh: 英文維基百科說，專門做來「唱」的缽，其製作與使用被認為是現代的現象。

tricks.body_en: Many people, one melody, one moment.
tricks.body_zh: 很多人、一條旋律、同一個時刻。

tricks.body_en: Short, steady, on every beat.
tricks.body_zh: 短、穩、每一拍一下。

tricks.body_en: Then the sound does not stop.
tricks.body_zh: 這樣聲音就不會中斷。

tricks.body_en: Teachings belong to each tradition’s teachers.
tricks.body_zh: 教義屬於各傳統的老師。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears and Voice · 保護耳朵與聲音

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. A knock is short and sharp, so it can feel louder than it is.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。敲擊又短又尖，會讓人覺得比實際更大聲。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: When you hum a long note, stay in a comfortable range and breathe whenever you need to. Stop if you feel dizzy.
safety.zh: 哼長音的時候，留在舒服的音域，需要就換氣。覺得頭暈就停下來。

materials.en: A desk and a soft object, such as a folded cloth, to knock on
materials.zh: 一張桌子和一個軟的東西，例如折起來的布，用來敲

materials.en: A classroom clock or a metronome
materials.zh: 教室的時鐘或節拍器

steps.en: One student knocks a slow, steady beat on the cloth, one knock every second.
steps.zh: 一位學生在布上敲一個緩慢穩定的拍子，每秒一下。

steps.en: The rest of the class hums one low note for six beats, then breathes for two beats. Everyone breathes at the same time.
steps.zh: 其他人哼一個低音六拍，再換氣兩拍。大家同時換氣。

steps.en: Try again, but let each small group breathe at a different time. Can you make the sound never stop?
steps.zh: 再來一次，但讓每一小組在不同時間換氣。你們能讓聲音不中斷嗎？

steps.en: Talk about it: what was hard? What did the steady knock help with?
steps.zh: 討論：什麼最難？穩定的敲擊幫了什麼忙？

activities.tip_en: Keep the knock soft. The knocker must not speed up or slow down, even when the hum changes.
activities.tip_zh: 敲得輕一點。敲的人不能加快或放慢，即使哼的聲音變了。

materials.en: Paper and a pen
materials.zh: 紙和筆

materials.en: A teacher or a guest who is willing to talk about their own community’s music
materials.zh: 一位願意聊聊自己社區音樂的老師或來賓

steps.en: Ask: how do people in your community behave when they listen to music at a special event?
steps.zh: 問：你們社區的人在特別的場合聽音樂時，怎麼表現？

steps.en: Write three ways to show respect when listening to music from a culture that is not your own.
steps.zh: 寫下三種聽別的文化的音樂時表示尊重的方法。

steps.en: If you visit a temple or another place of worship, follow the guidance of the people there.
steps.zh: 如果你去寺院或其他的宗教場所，聽那裡的人的指引。

steps.en: Share your list with the class.
steps.zh: 和全班分享你的清單。

activities.tip_en: Do not record or share someone’s music without asking them first.
activities.tip_zh: 沒有先問過，不要錄別人的音樂，也不要分享。
