lessons.sources_note_en: Names and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (November 2026). The long notes, breaths, and knocks are our own simple model; no recording, text, or tune of any tradition is used.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的名稱與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 11 月）；長音、換氣與敲擊是我們自己的簡單模型，沒有使用任何傳統的錄音、文字或曲調。

sources.en: In India it means singing the sacred words; in China it means chanting short verses or songs of praise
sources.zh: 在印度指歌詠法言，在中國則指唱頌短偈或歌讚
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「梵唄」

sources.en: Two shapes: a long straight fish hung in temple corridors for meals or to gather people; a round one used when chanting, placed on a table. The fish drum is a bamboo tube covered with fish skin at one end
sources.zh: 形制有二：一為挺直魚形，用來粥飯或集眾、警眾，懸掛在寺院走廊上。一為圓狀魚形，誦經時所用，放在案上。魚鼓簡板：魚鼓截竹為筒，一端蒙以魚皮
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「木魚」「魚鼓」

sources.en: Yinqing: a small bowl-shaped copper bell with a wooden handle, to attract attention. Qing: a hollow copper bowl-shaped instrument; also an ancient jade, stone, or metal chime. Weina: starts the chant and leads the group by striking the yinqing
sources.zh: 引磬：形如小碗，用銅製成，下附木柄，藉以引起大眾注意。磬：中空銅製，形狀像缽；古代用玉石或金屬製成的打擊樂器。維那：早晚課時擔任起腔唱誦、敲引磬領眾
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「引磬」「磬」「維那」

sources.en: Faqi: implements and instruments for monks and Daoist priests, such as bells, drums, cymbals, and fish. Morning and evening sessions: everyone in the temple goes to the main hall. Unison singing: two or more singers sing the same melody at the same time
sources.zh: 法器：僧道齋醮所需用具與樂器，如法劍、法盆、法鈴、法鼓與鐃、鈸、魚、罄等。朝暮課誦：全寺住眾必須上大殿禮拜。齊唱：兩位以上的歌唱者，不分聲部按照同一旋律同時演唱
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「法器」「朝暮課誦」「齊唱」

sources.en: In Chan, Seon, Zen and Thiền Buddhism, the wooden fish serve to maintain rhythm during chanting; hollow, the tone differs by size, material and the internal hollow; a rubber-coated mallet tip gives a muffled but clear sound; they rest on a cushion to prevent unpleasant knocking sounds
sources.zh: 在禪宗裡，木魚用來維持唱誦的節奏；中空，音色隨大小、材質與內部空腔而不同；橡膠包覆的木槌敲出悶悶但清楚的聲音；放在軟墊上避免難聽的碰撞聲

sources.en: Chinese Buddhist ritual chanting; the specific melodies and notes are traditionally only transmitted orally from generation to generation; in Taiwan two styles: Gushan faster with more ornamentation, Haichaoyin slow, relaxed and steady with a simpler melody; 課誦本並不提供旋律的標示
sources.zh: 漢傳佛教的儀式唱誦；旋律傳統上只靠口傳；台灣有鼓山調（較快、加花多）與海潮音（舒緩平穩、旋律較簡單）兩種；課誦本通常不標示旋律
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Fanbai” and 中文維基百科「梵唄」

sources.en: The intonation and style of the chant varies by tradition, with some preferring a more monotone chant and others a more melodic chanting; the manufacture and use of bowls specifically for “singing” is believed to be a modern phenomenon; the Chinese term qing historically referred to a lithophone used in state rituals
sources.zh: 唱誦的音調與風格因傳統而不同，有些偏單調、有些偏旋律；專門為「唱」而做的缽被認為是現代現象；「磬」歷史上指國家儀式用的石磬

sources.en: A bigger wooden fish has a lower pitch; temple wooden fish are placed on thick cushions; faqi means ritual implements used in both Buddhism and Daoism
sources.zh: 木魚的尺寸可有不同大小，體積越大音高越低；在廟宇中使用的木魚，會以厚軟墊置妥；法器泛指在佛教、道教裡供儀式使用的器具
sources.src: 中文維基百科「木魚」「法器」

sources.en: Stagger breathing is a technique for choir singers and wind instrument players as part of an ensemble, so that no breath gaps can be heard; unison is two or more musical parts that sound the same pitch
sources.zh: 輪流換氣是合唱與管樂合奏的技巧，讓聽不到換氣的空隙；齊唱是兩個以上的聲部唱同一個音高

sources.en: Taiwan's 12-year curriculum: arts (music) 音 E-Ⅱ-4, 音 P-Ⅱ-2, 音 P-Ⅲ-2, 音 A-Ⅲ-1
sources.zh: 十二年國民基本教育課程綱要藝術領域：音 E-Ⅱ-4、音 P-Ⅱ-2、音 P-Ⅲ-2、音 A-Ⅲ-1
sources.src: 國家教育研究院，十二年國教藝術領域課綱

sources.en: Safe listening: headphone volume to 60% of maximum, personal audio devices less than one hour a day
sources.zh: 安全聆聽：耳機音量不超過最大的 60%、個人音響裝置每天少於一小時

lessons.title: How Is a Song Put Together?
lessons.blurb_en: Build a song from colored blocks. Hear how the same block comes back exactly the same, and how a new block changes everything.
lessons.blurb_zh: 用色塊拼出一首歌。聽同一個色塊怎麼原封不動地回來，新的色塊又怎麼改變一切。
lessons.big_idea_en: A song is built from repetition and contrast. A section that comes back is repetition; a new section is contrast.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 一首歌由重複與對比搭起來。回來的段落是重複，新的段落是對比。

lab.how_en: We wrote three short tunes of two bars each: A, B, and C. Each one is a colored block. Add blocks in any order, then press play. Whenever a color comes back, the music comes back exactly the same. These tunes are our own. They are not any real song, and real songs are much longer and more varied.
lab.how_zh: 我們寫了三段各兩小節的短旋律：A、B、C。每一段是一個彩色的色塊。用任何順序加上色塊，再按播放。同一種顏色回來的時候，音樂原封不動地回來。這些旋律是我們自己寫的，不是任何真的歌，真正的歌長得多、也豐富得多。

paras: Song structure is the arrangement of a song. It is typically sectional, which means a song uses repeating forms. In musical form, the first statement of a musical idea is called A. Later contrasting sections are labeled B, C, D, and so on. Musical form shows the importance of two principles: repetition and contrast.

A verse of a song is a repeated sung melody where the words change from use to use. Each verse usually employs the same melody, while the lyrics usually change. A song structure in which all verses are sung to the same music is called strophic. Many folk and popular songs are strophic, including ballads and hymns.

The chorus, or refrain, is the part of the song that repeats at least once, both musically and lyrically. It usually retains the same set of lyrics every time its music appears, and it is normally the most memorable part. Verse–chorus form has two main sections that often contrast in melody, rhythm, harmony, and loudness. The two words chorus and refrain are often used interchangeably.

A bridge is a contrasting section that prepares for the return of the original material. It is a device used to break up the repetitive pattern of the song and keep the listener’s attention. The verse and the chorus are usually repeated throughout a song. The intro, the bridge, and the outro are usually used only once.

An introduction generally has just music and no words. An outro is a way of finishing or completing the song. Pop songs may have an introduction and an ending, but these parts are not essential to the identity of most songs. The dictionary also lists the interlude: music inserted between the main sections of a song.

There is no single order. Song form terminology is not standardized, and not every song has both a verse and a chorus. Some songs have only verses. Others, in the thirty-two-bar form, have an A section that shares the same melody three times with a contrasting B section. This is why we use the letters A, B, and C in this lesson, and not names. Can you hear what comes back and what is new?
paras_zh: 歌曲結構（song structure）是一首歌的編排。它通常是分段的，也就是一首歌使用重複的形式。在曲式裡，一個音樂想法第一次出現叫 A，之後對比的段落依序叫 B、C、D 等。曲式顯示了兩個原則的重要：重複與對比。
歌曲的一段「主歌」（verse）是一段重複演唱的旋律，歌詞每次都不同。每一段主歌通常用同一條旋律，歌詞則通常每段不同。所有詩節都用同一段音樂來唱的歌曲結構，叫做分節歌（strophic）。許多民謠和流行歌是分節歌，包括敘事歌謠與聖詩。
副歌（chorus 或 refrain）是歌曲裡至少重複一次的部分，音樂與歌詞都重複。每次它的音樂出現，歌詞通常都一樣，也通常是最容易記住的部分。主歌—副歌的形式有兩個主要段落，兩者常在旋律、節奏、和聲與力度上形成對比。chorus 和 refrain 這兩個詞常常互換使用。
橋段（bridge）是一個對比的段落，為原來的材料回來做準備。它是用來打破歌曲的重複模式、保持聽眾注意力的手法。主歌和副歌通常在整首歌中重複出現。前奏、橋段和結尾通常只用一次。
前奏一般只有音樂、沒有歌詞。結尾（outro）是結束或完成一首歌的方式。流行歌可以有前奏和結尾，但這些部分對大多數歌的特色並不是必要的。辭典還列了間奏：插在歌曲主要段落之間的音樂。
沒有唯一的順序。歌曲形式的術語並沒有標準化，也不是每首歌都同時有主歌和副歌。有些歌只有主歌。有的是三十二小節形式：A 段用同一條旋律三次，加上一個對比的 B 段。所以這一課用字母 A、B、C，不用名稱。你聽得出什麼回來了、什麼是新的嗎？
questions: What is the difference between repetition and contrast?
Does every song have both a verse and a chorus?
Why do we use the letters A, B, and C in this lesson?
answers: Repetition is when a section comes back; contrast is when a new, different section appears.
No. Some songs have only verses, and song form terminology is not standardized.
Because names like verse, chorus, and bridge are used differently in different songs; letters just show what comes back and what is new.

vocab.ex: The structure of a song is its arrangement.
vocab.exzh: 歌曲的結構就是它的編排。

vocab.ex: Each section has its own tune.
vocab.exzh: 每個段落有自己的旋律。

vocab.ex: The words change in every verse.
vocab.exzh: 每段主歌的歌詞都不同。

vocab.ex: Everyone sings the chorus together.
vocab.exzh: 大家一起唱副歌。

vocab.ex: The bridge sounds different from the rest.
vocab.exzh: 橋段聽起來跟其他部分不一樣。

vocab.ex: Repetition makes a tune easy to remember.
vocab.exzh: 重複讓旋律容易記住。

vocab.ex: A bridge adds contrast.
vocab.exzh: 橋段帶來對比。

vocab.ex: The outro finishes the song.
vocab.exzh: 結尾讓歌曲收尾。

quiz.q: In musical form, what is the first statement of a musical idea called?
What does a bridge usually do?
options: Contrasts, and prepares for the return of the original material

quiz.q: What is true about the chorus?
options: It usually keeps the same lyrics each time it comes back
It always has a different tune

quiz.q: If a song is A A B A, how many different sections does it have?
Why does this lesson use letters instead of names?
options: Song form terminology is not standardized

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It · 動手試試

parts.text_en: A is played twice, then B is different, then A returns exactly the same.
parts.text_zh: A 先彈兩次，B 不一樣，然後 A 原封不動地回來。

parts.text_en: Two sections take turns. Each one comes back once.
parts.text_zh: 兩個段落輪流出現，各回來一次。

parts.text_en: C is new and contrasts with the rest, and then B returns.
parts.text_zh: C 是新的，和其他的形成對比，然後 B 回來。

parts.text_en: A repeats, and the song ends on B, which ends on the home note.
parts.text_zh: A 重複，歌曲結束在 B，B 結束在主音。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then build your own with the blocks above, and play the game below.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後用上面的色塊拼自己的歌，再玩下面的遊戲。

formq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays a song made of blocks. Choose the order you heard. If you cannot hear the sound, press “What is in the music”.
formq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題播放一首用色塊拼的歌。選出你聽到的順序。如果聽不到聲音，按「音樂裡有什麼」。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The curriculum names repetition and contrast (grades 5–6) and writing a simple form. The words verse, chorus, and bridge do not appear in it, and grades 3–4 have no form vocabulary.
curric.lead_zh: 課綱在五、六年級寫到反覆與對比，以及簡易的曲式創作。「主歌」「副歌」「橋段」這些詞課綱裡沒有出現，三、四年級也沒有曲式的語彙。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 音樂美感原則，如：反覆、對比等。
items.note_en: Repetition and contrast are the two ideas of this lesson.
items.note_zh: 反覆與對比就是這一課的兩個想法。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 簡易創作，如：節奏創作、曲調創作、曲式創作等。
items.note_en: Arranging blocks is a simple way to create a form.
items.note_zh: 排色塊是創作曲式的一個簡單方法。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 相關音樂語彙，如曲調、調式等描述音樂元素之音樂術語，或相關之一般性用語。
items.note_en: Words like section and contrast help us describe what we hear.
items.note_zh: 段落、對比這樣的詞，幫助我們描述聽到的東西。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 音樂元素，如：節奏、力度、速度等。
items.note_en: Each block has its own tune; the elements are the ones named earlier.
items.note_zh: 每個色塊有自己的旋律；音樂元素是前面幾課學過的。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Letters, two words, a bridge in Chinese, and a round
culture_cards.title_zh: 字母、兩個詞、中文的橋段，和輪旋曲
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short notes about words and forms.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於詞彙與曲式的四個小註解。

cards.en: A, B, C, and no standard names
cards.body_en: Musical form uses letters. The first statement of an idea is A, and the contrasting sections that follow are labeled B, C, D, and so on. Song form terminology is not standardized, so one writer’s chorus may be another’s refrain. Taiwan’s dictionary defines 曲式 simply as the way a piece of music is built.
cards.body_zh: 曲式用字母。一個想法的第一次出現是 A，接著對比的段落依序標為 B、C、D 等。歌曲形式的術語並沒有標準化，所以一位作者說的 chorus，可能是另一位說的 refrain。台灣的辭典把「曲式」簡單定義為樂曲的構成方式。

cards.body_en: Taiwan’s list of music terms gives 副歌 for the pop-music chorus, and 疊句 or 副歌 for refrain. The dictionary’s 疊句 is a poetry word: a sentence used again and again in a poem, song text, or play. English Wikipedia adds that repeats of a refrain may use different words, and what makes a refrain recognizable is its melody.
cards.body_zh: 台灣的樂詞對照表，把通俗音樂的 chorus 對成「副歌」，refrain 對成「疊句」或「副歌」。辭典裡的「疊句」是詩詞用語：詩詞、戲曲、文章中重複使用的句子。英文維基百科補充說，refrain 的重複可以換字，讓它容易認出來的是旋律。

cards.en: A bridge, and a different 橋段
cards.body_en: In Chinese, 橋段 means a plot device in a story, a comic, or a film. It is not the bridge of a song. Taiwan’s list of music terms gives 過渡樂段 for the music word bridge. We keep the English word bridge in this lesson, and we tell you when the Chinese word means something else.
cards.body_zh: 中文的「橋段」是小說、漫畫、電影裡的表現手法，不是歌曲的 bridge。台灣的樂詞對照表，把音樂的 bridge 對成「過渡樂段」。這一課保留英文的 bridge，並在中文的詞意思不同時告訴你。

cards.body_en: The dictionary describes the rondo, also called 迴旋曲, as a piece with one main theme and several inserted sections. The main theme usually appears three times and alternates with the inserted sections, in the general form A–B–A–C–A. It shows the same idea as our blocks: one section keeps coming back, and new ones come between.
cards.body_zh: 辭典描述輪旋曲（也叫迴旋曲）是有一個主要主題和若干插入段的曲子。主題通常出現三次，與插入段輪流變換，一般形式是 A－B－A－C－A。它和我們的色塊是同一個想法：一個段落不斷回來，新的段落插在中間。

myths.myth_en: Every song has a verse and a chorus.
myths.myth_zh: 每首歌都有主歌和副歌。
myths.fact_en: Pop and rock songs often have both, but some songs have only verses.
myths.fact_zh: 流行與搖滾歌曲常常兩者都有，但有些歌只有主歌。

myths.myth_en: The bridge always comes after the second chorus.
myths.myth_zh: 橋段一定在第二次副歌之後。
myths.fact_en: It usually does in many songs, but not always. A bridge is a contrasting section that prepares for the return of the original material.
myths.fact_zh: 許多歌通常如此，但不一定。橋段是為原來材料回來做準備的對比段落。

myths.myth_en: The chorus always has exactly the same words.
myths.myth_zh: 副歌的歌詞一定一模一樣。
myths.fact_en: It usually does. But repeats of a refrain may use different words; the melody is what makes it recognizable.
myths.fact_zh: 通常如此。但 refrain 的重複可以換字，讓它容易認出來的是旋律。

myths.myth_en: Intro, bridge, and outro each appear in every song.
myths.myth_zh: 每首歌都有前奏、橋段和結尾。
myths.fact_en: They are not essential to the identity of most songs, and they are usually used only once.
myths.fact_zh: 它們對大多數歌的特色並不是必要的，而且通常只用一次。

tricks.title_zh: 同一個字母，同一段音樂
tricks.body_en: A returning section is repetition.
tricks.body_zh: 回來的段落是重複。

tricks.body_en: A new section is contrast.
tricks.body_zh: 新的段落是對比。

tricks.body_en: Use letters when you are not sure.
tricks.body_zh: 不確定的時候就用字母。

tricks.title_en: Not every song has a bridge
tricks.body_en: Many songs do not need one.
tricks.body_zh: 許多歌並不需要。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. When a song plays for a while, your ears can get tired without you noticing.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。歌曲播放一段時間後，耳朵可能累了你卻沒發現。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: Take a quiet break between games. Your ears like it.
safety.zh: 每個遊戲之間讓耳朵安靜休息一下。耳朵會喜歡。

activities.title_zh: 把你會唱的歌塗成色塊

materials.en: A short song your class already knows
materials.zh: 一首全班已經會的短歌

materials.en: Colored paper or crayons
materials.zh: 彩色紙或蠟筆

steps.en: Sing the song together and notice where the music comes back.
steps.zh: 全班一起唱，注意音樂在哪裡回來。

steps.en: Give each section its own color. Same music, same color.
steps.zh: 給每個段落一種顏色。一樣的音樂，一樣的顏色。

steps.en: Line up the colored blocks in order. What letters do you get?
steps.zh: 把色塊依序排好。你得到什麼字母？

steps.en: Compare with a friend. Did you hear the sections in the same places?
steps.zh: 和同學比一比。你們聽到的段落在同樣的地方嗎？

activities.tip_en: There may be more than one right answer. Let students explain what they heard.
activities.tip_zh: 答案可能不只一個。讓學生說明他們聽到了什麼。

materials.en: Hands for clapping or classroom instruments
materials.zh: 拍手或教室樂器

materials.en: Paper and a pen
materials.zh: 紙和筆

steps.en: In pairs, make a short rhythm of eight beats. This is block A.
steps.zh: 兩人一組，做一個八拍的短節奏。這是 A 色塊。

steps.en: Make a second rhythm that sounds different. This is block B.
steps.zh: 再做一個聽起來不同的節奏。這是 B 色塊。

steps.en: Perform them as A A B A. Then try A B A B.

sources.en: Song structure is the arrangement of a song; it is typically sectional; each verse usually employs the same melody while the lyrics usually change; the chorus usually retains the same set of lyrics every time its music appears; the bridge is a device used to break up the repetitive pattern; the verse, chorus and pre-chorus are usually repeated; the intro, bridge, and coda are usually only used once; an introduction contains just music and no words; intro and coda are not essential to the identity of most songs
sources.zh: 歌曲結構是歌曲的編排；通常是分段的；每段主歌通常用同一旋律、歌詞通常不同；副歌每次音樂出現歌詞通常相同；橋段用來打破重複的模式；主歌、副歌與預備副歌通常重複；前奏、橋段與結尾通常只用一次；前奏只有音樂沒有歌詞；前奏與結尾對大多數歌的特色並不必要

sources.en: The first statement of a musical idea is designated A. Subsequent contrasting sections are labeled B, C, D, and so on; the importance of the principles of repetition and contrast
sources.zh: 一個音樂想法的第一次出現標為 A，之後對比的段落依序標為 B、C、D；重複與對比兩個原則的重要

sources.en: A song structure in which all verses or stanzas of the text are sung to the same music; many folk and popular songs are strophic in form, including the twelve-bar blues, ballads, hymns and chants
sources.zh: 所有詩節都用同一段音樂來唱的歌曲結構；許多民謠與流行歌是分節歌，包括十二小節藍調、敘事歌謠、聖詩與唱誦

sources.en: Verse–chorus form consists of two main sections that often contrast melodically, rhythmically, harmonically and dynamically; songs which feature only a repeated verse are in simple verse form; predominant in rock music since the 1960s
sources.zh: 主歌—副歌形式有兩個主要段落，常在旋律、節奏、和聲與力度上形成對比；只有重複主歌的歌是簡單主歌形式；1960 年代以來在搖滾樂中佔主導

sources.en: A bridge is a contrasting section that prepares for the return of the original material section; although repeats of refrains may use different words, refrains are made recognizable by reusing the same melody; the terms chorus and refrain are often used interchangeably
sources.zh: 橋段是為原來材料回來做準備的對比段落；refrain 的重複可以換字，讓它容易認出來的是同一條旋律；chorus 與 refrain 常常互換使用

sources.en: The A sections all share the same melody (possibly with slight variations); the B section musically and lyrically contrasts the A sections; song form terminology is not standardized
sources.zh: A 段共用同一條旋律（可能略有變化）；B 段在音樂與歌詞上與 A 段對比；歌曲形式的術語沒有標準化

sources.en: Form: the way a piece of music is constructed. Interlude: music inserted between the main sections of a song or solo piece. Rondo: an instrumental piece with one main theme and several inserted sections, in the general form A–B–A–C–A, also called huixuanqu
sources.zh: 曲式：樂曲的構成方式。間奏：泛指歌曲或獨奏曲在主要樂段之間，所插入的音樂部分。輪旋曲：一種包含一個特定主題和若干插入段所構成的器樂曲，其一般形式為：A－B－A－C－A。也稱為「迴旋曲」

sources.en: A sentence used again and again in poems, plays, or writings is called a refrain sentence
sources.zh: 詩詞戲曲文章中，重複使用的句子，稱為「疊句」。

lessons.title: Why Is Bach Called the Father of Music?
lessons.blurb_en: Make a melody chase itself. Hear a canon, a unison, and two different tunes, and learn what the sources really say about Bach and his famous title.
lessons.blurb_zh: 讓一條旋律自己追自己。聽卡農、齊唱和兩條不同的旋律，再讀來源對巴哈和他著名的稱號到底怎麼說。
lessons.big_idea_en: In a canon, every voice sings the same tune, but each comes in later, so the tune chases itself. It works because the tune does not clash with itself.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 在卡農裡，每個聲部唱同一條旋律，但各晚一點進來，旋律就自己追自己。它之所以成立，是因為旋律和自己疊起來不會打架。

lab.how_en: We wrote one 16-beat tune. Choose how the voices sing: as a canon, together, or as two different tunes. For a canon, choose how many voices and how many beats apart they enter. Each voice has its own color on the piano roll. The tune is ours, written so that it never clashes with itself when it enters 2, 4, 6, or 8 beats late. It is not a tune by Bach or by anyone else.
lab.how_zh: 我們寫了一段 16 拍的旋律。選聲部怎麼唱：卡農、一起唱，或各唱不同的旋律。卡農的話，選幾個聲部、隔幾拍進來。鋼琴卷上每個聲部有自己的顏色。旋律是我們自己的，特別寫成晚 2、4、6 或 8 拍進來時都不會和自己打架。它不是巴哈或任何人的旋律。

paras: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) was a German composer and musician of the late Baroque period. He was born in Eisenach, the youngest child of a city musician, into a family that produced three to four generations of musicians. He was orphaned at the age of 10. He learned the violin, and he was also an organist. Our Lesson 13 shows what Baroque music is like.

In 1703 Bach became the organist at the New Church. He returned to Weimar as court organist in 1708, and he became a director of music in 1717. In 1723 he was appointed Thomaskantor, the director of church music in Leipzig, and he held that position for 27 years, until his death. He directed the St. Thomas School and provided four churches with music. A cantata was required for the church services on each Sunday, and his body of work includes more than 200 cantatas.

Bach’s music encompasses every genre of his time aside from opera. He wrote extensively for the organ and other keyboard instruments, and he also wrote orchestral and chamber music. He is known for his mastery of counterpoint. Many of his works use techniques like canon and fugue, which he did not invent but contributed to so fundamentally as to influence many followers.

A canon is a technique that employs a melody with one or more imitations of the melody. The first melody is the leader, and the imitating melody, in a different voice, is the follower. In the Taiwan dictionary, one voice comes first, and the other voices join with the same melody in turn, chasing one another to the last bar. A round is a limited type of canon: many voices sing exactly the same melody, each beginning at a different time. A voice here means a single melodic line.

Counterpoint is the relationship of two or more simultaneous musical lines. The lines depend on each other harmonically, yet they are independent in rhythm and melodic contour. A fugue is a technique in two or more voices built on a subject, which then sounds successively in each voice. The word comes from the Latin fuga, “flight”, and from the verbs for “to flee” and “to chase”. A fugue is closer to a style of composition than to a fixed form, so in this lesson we only play with canons.

Why is Bach called the father of music? In Taiwan’s dictionary he is “a founder of modern Western music” with the title “father of music”. Chinese Wikipedia says this label came into Chinese from Japanese scholars, has its limits, and is not yet widely accepted in the field. We could not find the title in English sources. What the sources do say is clear: after he died his reputation as a composer declined for a while, and he was remembered as an organist and a teacher. Haydn, Mozart, and Beethoven knew his music, and Felix Mendelssohn’s 1829 performance of the St. Matthew Passion precipitated the Bach Revival.
paras_zh: 約翰・塞巴斯蒂安・巴哈（1685–1750）是巴洛克晚期的德國作曲家與音樂家。他生在愛森納赫，是一位城市樂師最小的孩子，出身一個傳了三、四代音樂家的家族。他十歲就成了孤兒。他學過小提琴，也是管風琴家。第十三課介紹過巴洛克音樂是什麼樣子。
1703 年，巴哈成為新教堂的管風琴師。1708 年他回到威瑪擔任宮廷管風琴師，1717 年擔任音樂總監。1723 年他被任命為托馬斯教堂的歌手長（Thomaskantor），也就是萊比錫的教堂音樂總監，這個職位他做了 27 年，直到去世。他負責領導聖托馬斯學校，並為四間教堂提供音樂。每個星期天的禮拜都需要一首清唱劇，他的作品包括兩百多首清唱劇。
巴哈的音樂涵蓋了他那個時代除了歌劇以外的每一種體裁。他為管風琴與其他鍵盤樂器寫了很多，也寫管弦樂與室內樂。他以精通對位法聞名。他的許多作品用到卡農與賦格這些技法，他並沒有發明它們，但貢獻之大，影響了許多後來的人。
卡農是用一條旋律和它的一個或多個模仿所構成的技法。最先出現的旋律是導句，在不同聲部模仿的是答句。在台灣的辭典裡，一個聲部先出現，其他聲部以同樣的旋律依序加入，一直互相追逐，到最後一小節。輪唱是卡農的一種限定類型：許多聲部唱完全一樣的旋律，各自在不同的時間開始。這裡的「聲部」是指一條單獨的旋律線。
對位法是兩條或以上同時進行的旋律線之間的關係。這些線在和聲上互相依賴，在節奏與旋律輪廓上卻各自獨立。賦格是兩個或以上聲部、建立在一個主題上的技法，主題依序在每個聲部出現。這個詞來自拉丁文 fuga，「飛走」，也來自「逃跑」與「追趕」的動詞。賦格比較像一種作曲風格，而不是固定的形式，所以這一課我們只玩卡農。
巴哈為什麼被稱為音樂之父？在台灣的辭典裡，他是「近代西洋音樂的鼻祖」，有「音樂之父」的稱譽。中文維基百科說，這個稱呼是從日本學者傳入中文的，有它的侷限，也尚未在相關領域被廣泛接受。我們在英文的來源裡找不到這個稱號。來源說得清楚的是：他去世後，作為作曲家的名聲一度下滑，人們記得他是管風琴家與教師。海頓、莫札特和貝多芬都知道他的音樂，而孟德爾頌 1829 年演出《馬太受難曲》，促成了巴哈復興。
questions: What is the difference between a round and a canon?
Is “father of music” an established fact?
Why does our tune not clash with itself in a canon?
answers: A round is a limited type of canon in which all voices sing exactly the same melody, each beginning at a different time. A canon is the wider technique.
No. It is a title. Taiwan’s dictionary gives it, but Chinese Wikipedia says it is not widely accepted in the field, and we found it in no English source.
We wrote it so that the notes that sound together are always from the same set of notes. We tested it by computer for every entry time we offer.

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A title, a revival, another canon, and a big family
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個稱號、一次復興、另一首卡農，和一個大家庭
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories. We only write what the sources say.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事。我們只寫來源說的。

cards.body_en: Taiwan’s dictionary calls Bach a founder of modern Western music with the title “father of music”. Chinese Wikipedia says the label came from Japanese scholars’ books in the 1970s, and it is not widely accepted in the field. English sources do not use it. Beethoven called Bach the progenitor of harmony, and Mozart’s sentence about a “father” was about Bach’s son Carl Philipp Emanuel.
cards.body_zh: 台灣的辭典說巴哈是近代西洋音樂的鼻祖，有「音樂之父」的稱譽。中文維基百科說，這個稱呼來自日本學者的著作，經 1970 年代傳入中文，尚未在相關領域被廣泛接受。英文的來源沒有用它。貝多芬稱巴哈為「和聲之祖」，而莫札特那句關於「父親」的話，說的是巴哈的兒子卡爾・菲利普・艾曼努埃爾。

cards.body_en: After Bach died, his reputation as a composer initially declined, and he was remembered more as an organist and a teacher. In 1802 the first biography of him was published. Felix Mendelssohn’s 1829 performance of the St. Matthew Passion precipitated the Bach Revival, and in 1850 the Bach Society was founded to promote his music. He was not unknown in between: Haydn owned copies of his keyboard works, and Chinese Wikipedia says Mozart and Beethoven admired his music greatly.
cards.body_zh: 巴哈去世後，作為作曲家的名聲一度下滑，人們比較記得他是管風琴家與教師。1802 年出版了第一本他的傳記。孟德爾頌 1829 年演出《馬太受難曲》，促成了巴哈復興；1850 年成立了巴哈協會來推廣他的音樂。這中間他並不是無人知曉：海頓有他鍵盤作品的手抄本，中文維基百科說莫札特和貝多芬都對他推崇備至。

cards.body_en: The famous Canon in D is by Johann Pachelbel (1653–1706). It is a canon at the unison in three parts, with a fourth part as a ground bass throughout. Neither the date nor the circumstances of its composition are known. Taiwan’s dictionary itself gives Pachelbel’s Canon as its example of a canon. Bach did write canons, but that one is not his.
cards.body_zh: 著名的《D 大調卡農》是帕海貝爾（1653–1706）寫的。它是三個聲部的同度卡農，加上一個一直重複的第四聲部低音。它的寫作年代和情況都不知道。台灣的辭典自己就用帕海貝爾的《卡農》當卡農的例子。巴哈也寫過卡農，但那一首不是他的。

cards.body_en: English Wikipedia says Bach had twenty children, seven with his first wife and 13 with his second. Many did not survive to adulthood. Four of them, Wilhelm Friedemann, Carl Philipp Emanuel, Johann Christoph Friedrich, and Johann Christian, became composers. Late in life his eyesight failed, and he died after an unsuccessful eye surgery. He was not blind all his life.
cards.body_zh: 英文維基百科說巴哈有二十個孩子，第一任妻子七個、第二任十三個。許多孩子沒有活到成年。其中四位：威廉・弗里德曼、卡爾・菲利普・艾曼努埃爾、約翰・克里斯托夫・弗里德里希和約翰・克里斯蒂安，成了作曲家。他晚年視力衰退，死於一次不成功的眼睛手術。他並不是一輩子都看不見。

myths.myth_en: Bach wrote the famous “Canon in D”.
myths.myth_zh: 巴哈寫了著名的《D 大調卡農》。
myths.fact_en: It was written by Johann Pachelbel (1653–1706).
myths.fact_zh: 那是帕海貝爾（1653–1706）寫的。

myths.myth_en: Bach invented the canon and the fugue.
myths.myth_zh: 巴哈發明了卡農和賦格。
myths.fact_en: He did not invent them. He contributed to them so fundamentally as to influence many followers. The earliest known rounds date from 12th-century Europe.
myths.fact_zh: 他並沒有發明。他貢獻之大，影響了許多後來的人。最早已知的輪唱可以追溯到 12 世紀的歐洲。

myths.myth_en: Nobody played Bach until Mendelssohn.
myths.myth_zh: 在孟德爾頌之前沒人演奏巴哈。
myths.fact_en: His reputation declined for a while, but Haydn, Mozart, and Beethoven knew his music, and a biography came out in 1802. The 1829 performance precipitated the Bach Revival.
myths.fact_zh: 他的名聲一度下滑，但海頓、莫札特和貝多芬都知道他的音樂，1802 年也出版了傳記。1829 年的演出促成了巴哈復興。

myths.myth_en: Bach was blind.
myths.myth_zh: 巴哈是瞎的。
myths.fact_en: His eyesight failed late in life, and he died after an unsuccessful eye surgery. The sources do not say he was blind.
myths.fact_zh: 他晚年視力衰退，死於一次不成功的眼睛手術。來源沒有說他是瞎的。

tricks.body_en: Same tune, each voice enters later.
tricks.body_zh: 同一條旋律，每個聲部晚一點進來。

tricks.body_en: Exactly the same melody, entering in turn.
tricks.body_zh: 完全一樣的旋律，依序進來。

tricks.title_en: Fugue = a subject in every voice
tricks.body_en: More like a style than a form.
tricks.body_zh: 比較像風格，不是固定形式。

tricks.title_en: A title is not a fact
tricks.body_en: Ask who says it, and why.
tricks.body_zh: 問問是誰說的、為什麼。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. Four voices together are louder than one.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。四個聲部在一起比一個聲部大聲。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: When you sing a round, sing at a comfortable volume and stop if your throat hurts.
safety.zh: 唱輪唱的時候，用舒服的音量；喉嚨痛就停下來。

materials.en: Hands, or desks to tap softly
materials.zh: 雙手，或可以輕敲的桌子

materials.en: A steady beat counted aloud
materials.zh: 大聲數出來的穩定拍子

steps.en: The leader claps a short pattern of eight beats. Everyone listens.
steps.zh: 領頭的人拍一個八拍的短節奏。大家聽。

steps.en: Everyone claps the same pattern together: unison.
steps.zh: 大家一起拍同一個節奏：齊拍。

steps.en: Divide into two groups. Group 1 starts. Group 2 starts four beats later, with the same pattern: a canon.
steps.zh: 分成兩組。第一組開始，第二組晚四拍，用同樣的節奏：卡農。

steps.en: Try three groups, two beats apart. What changes?
steps.zh: 試試三組、隔兩拍。有什麼不同？

activities.tip_en: Keep the pattern simple, and count the beats aloud. A canon only works if everyone keeps the same steady beat.
activities.tip_zh: 節奏簡單一點，並把拍子數出來。大家保持同一個穩定的拍子，卡農才成立。

materials.en: A round your class already knows, or a short tune that can be sung one group after another
materials.zh: 全班已經會的輪唱，或可以一組接一組唱的短旋律

steps.en: Sing the whole tune together, once.
steps.zh: 全班一起唱一遍。

steps.en: Divide into groups. Each group starts after the previous group finishes the first line.
steps.zh: 分成幾組。每一組在前一組唱完第一句後開始。

steps.en: Keep going in a loop. When you want to end, one group at a time stops.
steps.zh: 一直循環。想結束的時候，一組一組停下來。

steps.en: Talk about it: could you hear your own line? What helped?
steps.zh: 討論：你聽得到自己的線條嗎？什麼幫了你？

activities.tip_en: A round has no fixed ending, so decide in advance how you will stop.
activities.tip_zh: 輪唱沒有固定的結尾，所以先決定怎麼停。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (November 2026). The tune and the way the voices enter are our own simple model, tested by computer; no tune by Bach or anyone else is used.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的名稱、年代與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 11 月）；旋律與聲部進入的方式是我們自己的簡單模型，用電腦測試過；沒有使用巴哈或任何人的旋律。

sources.en: 31 March [O.S. 21 March] 1685 – 28 July 1750; born in Eisenach, the youngest child of the city musician; three to four generations of musicians; orphaned at age 10; organist at the New Church 1703; court organist at Weimar 1708; Kapellmeister 1717; Thomaskantor in Leipzig 1723, held for 27 years; more than 200 cantatas; every genre of his time aside from opera; counterpoint, canon and fugue, which he did not invent; twenty children; died from complications due to unsuccessful eye surgery; reputation initially declined; Mendelssohn's 1829 performance precipitated the Bach Revival
sources.zh: 1685 年 3 月 31 日（舊曆 3 月 21 日）至 1750 年 7 月 28 日；生於愛森納赫、城市樂師最小的孩子；三、四代音樂家；十歲成孤兒；1703 年新教堂管風琴師；1708 年威瑪宮廷管風琴師；1717 年音樂總監；1723 年萊比錫歌手長、做了 27 年；兩百多首清唱劇；涵蓋當時除歌劇外所有體裁；對位法、卡農與賦格（他沒有發明）；二十個孩子；死於不成功的眼睛手術；名聲一度下滑；孟德爾頌 1829 年的演出促成巴哈復興

sources.en: A canon is a contrapuntal compositional technique that employs a melody with one or more imitations of the melody; the initial melody is called the leader, the imitative melody the follower; a round is a limited type of canon in which multiple voices sing exactly the same melody, each voice beginning at different times; the earliest known rounds date from 12th-century Europe
sources.zh: 卡農是用一條旋律和它的一個或多個模仿構成的對位技法；最初的旋律是導句，模仿的是答句；輪唱是卡農的限定類型，多個聲部唱完全一樣的旋律、各自在不同的時間開始；最早已知的輪唱來自十二世紀的歐洲

sources.en: A fugue is a contrapuntal, polyphonic compositional technique in two or more voices, built on a subject which then sounds successively in each voice; from Latin fuga; the fugue is closer to a style of composition rather than a structural form; counterpoint is the relationship of two or more simultaneous musical lines (voices)
sources.zh: 賦格是兩個或以上聲部、建立在主題上的對位複音技法，主題依序在每個聲部出現；來自拉丁文 fuga；賦格比較像作曲風格而非結構形式；對位法是兩條或以上同時進行的旋律線（聲部）之間的關係

sources.en: Pachelbel's Canon (also known as Canon in D, P 37) is an accompanied canon by German Baroque composer Johann Pachelbel (1653–1706); a true canon at the unison in three parts, with a fourth part as a ground bass; neither the date nor the circumstances of its composition are known
sources.zh: 帕海貝爾《卡農》（又稱 D 大調卡農）是德國巴洛克作曲家帕海貝爾（1653–1706）的伴奏卡農；三個聲部的同度卡農，加一個固定低音聲部；寫作年代與情況都不知道

sources.en: Personal name (1685–1750), German composer ... also a founder of modern Western music, with the title “father of music”; also translated as Bach
sources.zh: 人名。（西元1685～1750）德國作曲家……也是近代西洋音樂的鼻祖，有音樂之父的稱譽。也譯作「巴赫」。
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「巴哈」

sources.en: Canon: one voice comes first and the others join in turn with the same melody, chasing to the last bar. Round: a vocal piece in canon at the unison. Voice: a part into which music or singing is divided by pitch
sources.zh: 卡農：一個聲部先出現，其他聲部以同樣旋律依序加入，自始自終追逐著，直到最後一小節。輪唱曲：用同度卡農手法寫成的聲樂曲。聲部：在音樂演奏和歌唱中，根據聲音的高低不同，分成若干部分
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「卡農」「輪唱」「聲部」「對位」

sources.en: Bach is called “father of music”; this label has limits and is not widely accepted in the field; Japanese scholars called him that; cataracts gradually took his eyesight; Mendelssohn's 1829 performance made musicians take Bach's music seriously; the original meaning of fugue is “chase” and “flight”
sources.zh: 將巴哈稱為「音樂之父」。這個稱法有其侷限，也尚未在相關領域被廣泛接受；可見日本學者如海老澤敏、門馬直美等，將巴哈稱為「音樂之父」；白內障使巴哈的視力逐漸喪失；孟德爾頌 1829 年才使樂壇正視巴哈音樂的價值；賦格的原意是「追逐」和「飛翔」
sources.src: 中文維基百科「約翰・塞巴斯蒂安・巴赫」「卡農」「賦格」

sources.en: canon 卡農；fugue 復格、復格曲；counterpoint 對位法；voice 人聲、聲部、聲音；organ 管風琴；cantata 清唱劇
sources.zh: canon; fugue (fugue is rendered as fuge, fuge piece in this list); counterpoint; voice: human voice, part, sound; organ; cantata

sources.zh: 十二年國民基本教育課程綱要藝術領域：音 E-Ⅲ-1（輪唱、合唱）、音 A-Ⅲ-1（作曲家）、音 A-Ⅲ-3（反覆、對比）、音 A-Ⅳ-1；創作技法：模仿、反覆、對比

sources.zh: 安全聆聽：耳機音量不超過最大的 60%、個人音響裝置每天少於一小時

lessons.title: How Did Beethoven Compose After He Lost His Hearing?
lessons.title_zh: 貝多芬聽不見了，怎麼還能作曲？
lessons.blurb_en: Read notes on a staff and hear them in your head. Try silent bars, guess a tune’s shape from the page, and read what the sources say about Beethoven.
lessons.blurb_zh: 讀五線譜上的音，在腦子裡聽。試試無聲的小節、從譜上猜旋律的樣子，再讀來源對貝多芬怎麼說。
lessons.big_idea_en: A score is music written down, so a skilled reader can hear it in the mind. That ability is one reason a composer can keep working when hearing becomes harder.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 樂譜是寫下來的音樂，所以熟練的讀譜者可以在腦子裡聽到它。這種能力，是作曲家在聽力變差時仍能工作的原因之一。

lab.how_en: Here is a tune of four bars, written on a staff. It is our own tune, not Beethoven’s or anyone else’s. Choose bars to make silent: their notes turn gray and make no sound. Press play, read the gray notes, and try to hear them in your head. Then press “Reveal” to check.
lab.how_zh: 這是一段四小節的旋律，寫在五線譜上。它是我們自己的旋律，不是貝多芬或任何人的。選幾個小節設成無聲：它們的音會變灰、不發聲。按播放，讀那些灰色的音，試著在腦子裡聽。再按「揭曉」對答案。

paras: Musical notation is any system used to visually represent music, and the process of interpreting it is often called reading music. Sheet music is a written or printed form of musical notation that uses symbols to indicate pitches, rhythms, or chords. The word score is a common alternative term. On a staff, a set of horizontal lines, usually five, each line and space represents a different pitch. Lesson 5 shows how to read it.

Sight-reading is the practice of reading and performing a piece in music notation. Highly skilled musicians can sight-read silently: they look at the printed music and hear it in their heads without playing or singing. Audiation is a term coined by Edwin Gordon in 1975 for comprehension and internal realization of music, the sensation of hearing sound when it is not physically present. Skilled composers and conductors have this ability, with Beethoven being a noted historical example.

Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist. He was baptized on December 17, 1770, in Bonn, and he died on March 26, 1827. There is no authentic record of the date of his birth. He was a musical prodigy, and at age 21 he moved to Vienna, which became his base. Our Lesson 13 shows where he fits between the Classical and the Romantic.

Around 1798, Beethoven began to lose his hearing, as he told a friend in 1815. The decline was gradual, and it came with a severe form of tinnitus, a ringing in the ear. Historians are not completely sure why it happened. One of his students reported that he could still hear speech and music normally until 1812. Contrary to common belief, Beethoven never became totally deaf. In his final years he could still distinguish low tones and sudden loud sounds.

Beethoven’s hearing loss did not prevent him from composing music. From 1814 he used ear trumpets for conversation. Later his hearing seriously deteriorated, and he and the people talking to him wrote in notebooks, called conversation books. His late period, 1812 to 1827, included some of his most innovative works. His Ninth Symphony was first performed on May 7, 1824, in Vienna. He stood by the conductor, beating time, though the conductor had told the performers to follow him instead. A singer turned him around to see the applause he could not hear.

Hearing loss is either a partial inability to hear, or a total inability called deafness. Evelyn Glennie, a Scottish percussionist, has been profoundly deaf since childhood, and she performs as a soloist with many orchestras. She plays barefoot to feel the music, and she says deafness is largely misunderstood by the public. For us, the lesson is about reading music and imagining it. It is also a reminder to protect our ears: keep headphones at no more than 60% of maximum, and limit personal audio players to an hour a day.
paras_zh: 樂譜（musical notation）是用視覺表現音樂的任何系統，解讀它的過程常被稱為讀譜。譜（sheet music）是手寫或印刷的記譜形式，用符號標出音高、節奏或和弦。「score」是常用的另一個詞。在五線譜上，一組水平的線（通常五條），每一條線和每一個間，代表不同的音高。第五課教你怎麼讀。
視奏（sight-reading）是讀著譜演奏一首曲子的做法。非常熟練的音樂家可以無聲地視奏：看著印好的譜，在腦子裡聽到，不用演奏也不用唱。「內在聽覺」（audiation）是戈登（Edwin Gordon）在 1975 年提出的詞，指對音樂的理解與內在實現，也就是聲音不在眼前時，卻有聽到聲音的感覺。熟練的作曲家和指揮有這種能力，貝多芬是歷史上著名的例子。
路德維希・范・貝多芬是德國的作曲家與鋼琴家。他在 1770 年 12 月 17 日於波昂受洗，1827 年 3 月 26 日去世。他出生的日期沒有可靠的紀錄。他是音樂神童，21 歲搬到維也納，那裡成了他的根據地。第十三課介紹過他在古典與浪漫之間的位置。
大約 1798 年，貝多芬開始失去聽力，這是他 1815 年告訴一位朋友的。聽力是慢慢下降的，還伴隨嚴重的耳鳴（耳朵裡的鳴叫聲）。歷史學者並不完全確定原因。他的一位學生說，一直到 1812 年，他還能正常聽見談話與音樂。和一般人的想法相反，貝多芬從來沒有完全失聰。在最後的幾年，他仍能分辨低音和突然的巨響。
貝多芬的聽力損失並沒有妨礙他作曲。1814 年起，他用助聽喇叭來交談。後來聽力嚴重惡化，他和說話的人就在筆記本上寫字，這些筆記本叫「談話簿」。他的晚期（1812 到 1827 年）有一些他最創新的作品。第九號交響曲 1824 年 5 月 7 日在維也納首演。他站在指揮旁邊打拍子，但指揮已告訴演奏者要跟著指揮，不要跟他。一位歌手把他轉過來，讓他看到他聽不到的掌聲。
聽力損失，可以是部分聽不到，也可以是完全聽不到，叫做失聰。愛芙琳・葛蘭妮（Evelyn Glennie）是蘇格蘭的打擊樂家，從小就深度失聰，她以獨奏家身分和許多樂團演出。她赤腳演奏，為了「感覺音樂」，她也說大眾對失聰有很大的誤解。對我們來說，這一課是關於讀譜與想像音樂，也提醒我們保護耳朵：耳機音量不超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天用不超過一小時。
questions: What is a score?
Was Beethoven totally deaf?
What does it mean to “hear music in your head”?
answers: A score is the written form of music, with symbols that show pitches and rhythms. It is another word for sheet music.
No. Wikipedia says that, contrary to common belief, he never became totally deaf. In his final years he could still hear low tones and sudden loud sounds.
It means looking at written music and imagining how it sounds without playing or singing. Skilled musicians can do this, which is called sight-reading silently.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It · 動手試試

parts.zh: 想像第 2 和第 4 小節
parts.text_en: Read the gray notes while they pass in silence, and hear them in your head.
parts.text_zh: 灰色的音靜靜地過去，一邊讀、一邊在腦子裡聽。

parts.zh: 想像第 1 和第 3 小節
parts.text_en: This time the tune begins in silence. Can you imagine the beginning from the page?
parts.text_zh: 這次旋律從無聲開始。你能從譜上想像開頭嗎？

parts.zh: 只有第 1 小節有聲音
parts.text_en: A harder challenge: read the last three bars, and hear them only in your head.
parts.text_zh: 比較難的挑戰：讀後面三個小節，只在腦子裡聽。

parts.text_en: Every note sounds. Did the music in your head match?
parts.text_zh: 每個音都響。你腦子裡的音樂一樣嗎？

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the game below: read four notes, and decide the shape of the tune before you hear it.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試下面的遊戲：讀四個音，在聽到之前先判斷旋律的樣子。

contourq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one shows four notes on a staff. Decide whether the tune climbs, falls, makes a hill or a valley, or zigzags. Then press “Listen to check”. The game works without sound.
contourq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題在五線譜上放四個音。判斷旋律是往上、往下、山峰、山谷，還是鋸齒。然後按「聽聽看」對答案。沒有聲音也能玩。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The curriculum names reading scores, notation, and composers. The words Beethoven, hearing, and score as a noun do not appear in its music items, and it has no wording about deaf or hard-of-hearing students.
curric.lead_zh: 課綱寫到讀譜、記譜法與作曲家。「貝多芬」「聽覺」「聽力」這些詞，課綱的音樂項目裡沒有出現，課綱也沒有關於聽障學生的字句。

items.note_zh: 讀五線譜是這一課的基礎。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）

items.note_en: Notation comes in many forms, not only the staff.
items.note_zh: 記譜法有很多種，不只五線譜。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）

items.note_en: Composers and the background of their music.
items.note_zh: 作曲家與他們音樂的創作背景。

items.area: 藝術領域・學習表現（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 能透過聽唱、聽奏及讀譜，進行歌唱及演奏，以表達情感。
items.note_en: Learning to sing and play from the page.
items.note_zh: 學著從譜上唱與奏。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Not totally deaf, notebooks, another musician, and careful words
culture_cards.title_zh: 不是完全失聰、筆記本、另一位音樂家，和小心的用詞
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories. We only write what the sources say, and we leave out what they do not.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事。我們只寫來源說的，來源沒說的就不寫。

cards.body_en: Many people believe Beethoven was totally deaf. Wikipedia says, contrary to common belief, that he never became totally deaf, and that in his final years he could still distinguish low tones and sudden loud sounds. One of his students reported that he could hear speech and music normally until 1812. The sources do not agree on every word, so we say only that he could hear very little late in life.
cards.body_zh: 許多人以為貝多芬完全失聰。維基百科說，和一般人的想法相反，他從來沒有完全失聰，最後幾年他仍能分辨低音與突然的巨響。他的一位學生說，一直到 1812 年他還能正常聽見談話與音樂。各來源並非每個字都一致，所以我們只說他晚年能聽到的很少。

cards.body_en: From 1814 Beethoven used ear trumpets designed by Johann Nepomuk Maelzel for conversation, which strengthen the sound reaching the eardrum. Later he and the people he talked to wrote in notebooks. These conversation books are a rich written resource for his life from that period on, and they contain discussions about music, business, and personal life. A piano maker also tried a special resonator for him, but it failed in this task.
cards.body_zh: 從 1814 年起，貝多芬用梅爾策爾（Maelzel）設計的助聽喇叭來交談，它能增強傳到耳膜的聲音。後來他和說話的人在筆記本上寫字。這些談話簿是那段時期之後他生活的豐富文字資料，內容有音樂、事務與私人生活的討論。一位鋼琴製造者也為他試過特別的共鳴裝置，但沒有成功。

cards.body_en: Evelyn Glennie is a Scottish percussionist who has been profoundly deaf since childhood, having started to lose her hearing at the age of eight. This does not inhibit her ability to perform. She plays barefoot to feel the music, and her teacher taught her to hear with parts of her body other than her ears. She says deafness is largely misunderstood by the public.
cards.body_zh: 愛芙琳・葛蘭妮是蘇格蘭的打擊樂家，從小就深度失聰，八歲開始失去聽力。這並不妨礙她演出。她赤腳演奏來感覺音樂，她的老師教她用耳朵以外的身體部位去聽。她說大眾對失聰有很大的誤解。

cards.body_en: Taiwan’s dictionary notes that the older word for a person who cannot hear is now replaced by 聽覺障礙者, “a person with a hearing impairment”. The same dictionary defines 失聰 as losing one’s hearing. In this lesson we say hearing loss, or lost much of his hearing, and we do not use labels. We also do not guess at causes the sources are not sure about.
cards.body_zh: 台灣的辭典說，稱呼聽不到的人的舊詞，現在改稱「聽覺障礙者」。同一本辭典把「失聰」解釋為失去聽力。這一課我們說「聽力損失」或「失去很多聽力」，不用標籤。來源不確定的原因，我們也不猜。

myths.myth_en: Beethoven was totally deaf.
myths.myth_zh: 貝多芬完全失聰。
myths.fact_en: Wikipedia says that, contrary to common belief, he never became totally deaf. In his final years he could still hear low tones and sudden loud sounds.
myths.fact_zh: 維基百科說，和一般人的想法相反，他從來沒有完全失聰。最後幾年他仍能聽到低音和突然的巨響。

myths.myth_en: He composed everything after he lost his hearing.
myths.myth_zh: 他所有的作品都是失聰後寫的。
myths.fact_en: His hearing began to decline around 1798, and his First Symphony premiered in 1800. One student said he could hear normally until 1812.
myths.fact_zh: 他的聽力約在 1798 年開始下降，第一號交響曲 1800 年首演。有學生說他到 1812 年還能正常聽。

myths.myth_en: He conducted the premiere of the Ninth Symphony.
myths.myth_zh: 他指揮了第九號交響曲的首演。
myths.fact_en: He stood by the conductor, Michael Umlauf, beating time, although Umlauf had warned the singers and orchestra to ignore him.
myths.fact_zh: 他站在指揮烏姆勞夫旁邊打拍子，但烏姆勞夫已警告歌手與樂團不要理他。

myths.myth_en: Only Beethoven could hear music in his head.
myths.myth_zh: 只有貝多芬能在腦子裡聽音樂。
myths.fact_en: Highly skilled musicians can sight-read silently, hearing the music in their heads. Beethoven is a noted historical example, not the only one.
myths.fact_zh: 非常熟練的音樂家可以無聲地視奏，在腦子裡聽音樂。貝多芬是歷史上著名的例子，不是唯一的。

tricks.title_en: A score is music on paper
tricks.body_en: Symbols for pitch and rhythm.
tricks.body_zh: 音高與節奏的符號。

tricks.body_en: Practice makes it stronger.
tricks.body_zh: 練習會讓它更強。

tricks.body_en: Say hearing loss, not labels.
tricks.body_zh: 說聽力損失，不貼標籤。

tricks.body_en: 60% volume, an hour a day.
tricks.body_zh: 音量 60%、每天一小時。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: Wikipedia says about half of hearing loss around the world is preventable through public health measures. Taking care of your ears now is a good start.
safety.zh: 維基百科說，全球約一半的聽力損失可以靠公共衛生措施預防。現在就照顧耳朵，是個好的開始。

materials.en: Four notes written on a staff, on the board or on paper
materials.zh: 寫在黑板或紙上五線譜的四個音

materials.en: A keyboard or a recorder, if you have one
materials.zh: 鍵盤或直笛，如果有的話

steps.en: Show four notes on a staff. Do not play them.
steps.zh: 展示五線譜上的四個音。先不要彈。

steps.en: Ask: does the tune climb, fall, make a hill, a valley, or a zigzag? Vote with your hands.
steps.zh: 問：旋律是往上、往下、山峰、山谷，還是鋸齒？用手勢投票。

steps.en: Play the notes and check. Who read it correctly?
steps.zh: 彈出來對答案。誰讀對了？

steps.en: Write a new four-note tune, and let a partner read it before they hear it.
steps.zh: 寫一段新的四個音的旋律，讓同伴在聽到之前先讀。

activities.tip_en: Stay on the shape only. Names of notes can come later.
activities.tip_zh: 先只看形狀。音名之後再學。

materials.en: A short tune your class already knows well
materials.zh: 全班已經很熟的短旋律

materials.en: A steady beat counted aloud
materials.zh: 大聲數出來的穩定拍子

steps.en: Sing the tune together with the beat.
steps.zh: 全班跟著拍子一起唱。

steps.en: Choose one phrase to be silent. Everyone keeps the beat and imagines singing it.
steps.zh: 選一個樂句變成無聲。大家保持拍子，並在心裡想像唱它。

steps.en: Join in again at the next phrase, together. Did you come in at the same time?
steps.zh: 到下一個樂句，一起再加入。你們同時進來了嗎？

steps.en: Talk about it: how did you know when to come in?
steps.zh: 討論：你怎麼知道什麼時候要進來？

activities.tip_en: Count the beats silently in your head. That is the same skill as hearing the notes in your head.
activities.tip_zh: 在腦子裡默數拍子。這和在腦子裡聽音符是同一種能力。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (November 2026). The tune and the games are our own; no tune by Beethoven or anyone else is used. We do not state a cause for his hearing loss, because the sources are not sure.
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的名稱、年代與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 11 月）；旋律與遊戲是我們自己的，沒有使用貝多芬或任何人的旋律。我們不寫他聽力損失的原因，因為來源也不確定。

sources.en: baptised 17 December 1770 – 26 March 1827; there is no authentic record of the date of his birth; born in Bonn; at age 21 he moved to Vienna; hearing loss began 1798 as he told Charles Neate in 1815; a severe form of tinnitus; Czerny: could still hear speech and music normally until 1812; contrary to common belief, Beethoven never became totally deaf; in his final years, still able to distinguish low tones and sudden loud sounds; hearing loss did not prevent him from composing; ear-trumpets from 1814; conversation books; the Ninth first performed 7 May 1824; he stood by the conductor Umlauf beating time; Unger turned Beethoven around to see the applause he could not hear; late period 1812–1827
sources.zh: 1770 年 12 月 17 日受洗至 1827 年 3 月 26 日；沒有可靠的出生日期紀錄；生於波昂；21 歲搬到維也納；1798 年聽力開始下降（1815 年告訴 Neate）；嚴重耳鳴；車爾尼說他到 1812 年還能正常聽到談話與音樂；和一般人的想法相反，貝多芬從來沒有完全失聰；最後幾年仍能分辨低音與突然的巨響；聽力損失沒有妨礙他作曲；1814 年起用助聽喇叭；談話簿；第九號 1824 年 5 月 7 日首演；他站在指揮烏姆勞夫旁打拍子；溫格把貝多芬轉過來看他聽不到的掌聲；晚期 1812–1827

sources.en: Sight-reading is the practice of reading and performing a piece in a music notation; highly skilled musicians can sight-read silently, hearing it in their heads; audiation: comprehension and internal realization of music, the sensation of hearing sound when it is not physically present
sources.zh: 視奏是讀著記譜法演奏一首曲子的做法；非常熟練的音樂家可以無聲地視奏，在腦子裡聽；內在聽覺：對音樂的理解與內在實現，聲音不在眼前時有聽到聲音的感覺

sources.en: Musical notation is any system used to visually represent music; sheet music uses musical symbols to indicate pitches, rhythms, or chords; the term score is a common alternative term; skilled composers and conductors have this ability, with Beethoven being a noted historical example
sources.zh: 記譜法是用視覺表現音樂的任何系統；譜用音樂符號標示音高、節奏或和弦；score 是常用的另一個詞；熟練的作曲家與指揮有這種能力，貝多芬是歷史上著名的例子

sources.en: Hearing loss is either a partial inability to hear, or a total inability termed deafness; WHO recommends limiting personal audio players to an hour a day; about half of hearing loss globally is preventable; Glennie has been profoundly deaf since childhood, started to lose her hearing at age 8, plays barefoot to feel the music, and contends that deafness is largely misunderstood by the public
sources.zh: 聽力損失是部分聽不到，或完全聽不到（失聰）；世界衛生組織建議個人音響每天用一小時；全球約一半的聽力損失可以預防；葛蘭妮從小深度失聰、八歲開始失去聽力、赤腳演奏來感覺音樂，並說大眾對失聰有很大的誤解

sources.en: Personal name (1770–1827), German composer, known as the “Saint of Music”. (Other clauses in the dictionary differ from Wikipedia and are not used on this page.)
sources.zh: 人名。（西元1770～1827）德國作曲家……世稱為「樂聖」。（辭典其他的句子與維基百科不同，本頁不引用。）

sources.zh: 五線譜：在五條等距平行橫線上標記音符，以表示音樂高低、節奏等性質的樂譜。失聰：失去聽力。聾人（ID 67420）：聽覺有障礙或完全聽不見的人，今改稱「聽覺障礙者」。

lessons.title: Who Wrote the Songs Taiwan Still Sings?
lessons.title_zh: 誰寫了台灣人到現在還在唱的歌？
lessons.blurb_en: Meet Teng Yu-hsien, a Taiwanese composer born in 1906, and write your own tune on the five-note scale. We name his songs and tell his story, and we leave out his melodies and words.
lessons.blurb_zh: 認識 1906 年出生的台灣作曲家鄧雨賢，再用五聲音階寫自己的旋律。我們說他的歌名和故事，不放他的旋律與歌詞。
lessons.big_idea_en: A song has people behind it: a composer, often a lyricist, and singers. On the five-note scale, almost any tune you write sounds smooth, because none of its notes are a half step apart.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 一首歌背後有人：作曲家、常常還有作詞的人，和唱歌的人。在五聲音階上，你寫的旋律幾乎都聽起來順，因為它的音之間沒有半音。

lab.title_en: Write a Tune on Five Notes
lab.how_en: Write your own tune: eight steps, five notes: C, D, E, G, and A. Click a square to place a note, and click it again to take it away. The list under the grid tells you what your tune does. It does not give a score. You can also show the two missing notes, F and B, and hear what a half step sounds like. The starting tunes are ours. They are not songs by Teng Yu-hsien or by anyone else.
lab.how_zh: 寫你自己的旋律：八格、五個音：C、D、E、G、A。點一個方格放音，再點一次取消。格子下面的清單告訴你，你的旋律做了什麼，它不打分數。你也可以顯示缺少的兩個音 F 和 B，聽聽半音是什麼聲音。現成的旋律是我們自己寫的，不是鄧雨賢或任何人的歌。

paras: A pentatonic scale is a musical scale with five notes per octave. Starting on C, the major pentatonic scale is C, D, E, G, and A. Pentatonic scales were developed independently by many ancient civilizations, and they are still used in various musical styles today. The black keys on a piano keyboard make a pentatonic scale. In Taiwan’s dictionary, the five tones 宮, 商, 角, 徵, and 羽 are the five notes of the old Chinese scale. We tested our own notes by computer: no two of the notes C, D, E, G, and A are a half step apart.

Teng Yu-hsien was a Hakka composer, born on July 21, 1906, in the Longtan area of Taoyuan, in Japanese-ruled Taiwan. He died on June 11, 1944. At fifteen he entered the Taipei Normal School, a teacher-training school, and studied music there. He played the cello, the violin, the piano, and the mandolin. In 1925 he became a teacher at a public school. He later studied the theory of composition at a music college in Tokyo, and he returned to Taiwan in 1930.

In 1933, when he was 28, a Columbia record company invited him to be its full-time composer, and in the same year he wrote songs such as “Longing for the Spring Breeze” and “Worry on a Moonlit Night”. Four of his best-known songs, “Rainy Night Flower”, “Longing for the Spring Breeze”, “Worry on a Moonlit Night”, and “Four Seasons Red”, are grouped together under the name 四月望雨. In 1940 he left the record industry and went back to teaching, at a school in Xinzhu.

The Hakka Affairs Council says he left behind nearly 100 songs, many of which continue to be sung today. “Longing for the Spring Breeze” was voted the most popular 100-year-old song in Taiwan. Chinese Wikipedia describes the melody of this song as using the pentatonic gong mode. But who wrote the words? The words of “Longing for the Spring Breeze” were written by Li Lin-chiu, and the words of “Rainy Night Flower” by Chou Tien-wang. A song often has a composer and a lyricist, who are different people.

“Rainy Night Flower” began as a children’s song called “Spring”. It was written in 1933 for Taiwanese children by the writer Liao Han-chen, and he gave it to Teng to set to music. Many of Teng’s songs were later banned, and some were rewritten into Japanese. A record of a Japanese popular song that was thought to be lost was rediscovered by a collector in 2007. An asteroid, 255989 Dengyushian, was named in his honor.

Why do we not play his tunes or print his words here? Taiwan’s copyright law protects a work during the author’s life and 50 years after death, and the term ends on the last day of that year. By this rule, a composer who died in 1944 has been out of copyright since 1995, but the lyricists lived longer, so their words are still protected. Recordings and arrangements have their own terms. A composer’s moral rights, such as the right to be named and to keep a work from being distorted, continue even after death. So this lesson tells you the facts and the song names, and you write your own tune.
paras_zh: 五聲音階是每個八度裡有五個音的音階。從 C 開始，大調五聲音階是 C、D、E、G、A。五聲音階是許多古老的文明各自獨立發展出來的，到今天仍用在各種音樂風格裡。鋼琴的黑鍵組成的也是一個五聲音階。在台灣的辭典裡，宮、商、角、徵、羽五個音，是古代中國音階的五個音。我們用電腦測試過自己的音：C、D、E、G、A 當中，任何兩個音都不是相差半音。
鄧雨賢是客家作曲家，1906 年 7 月 21 日出生在日本統治下的台灣，桃園龍潭一帶。他在 1944 年 6 月 11 日去世。十五歲，他進了臺北師範學校，在那裡學音樂。他會拉大提琴、小提琴，也會彈鋼琴和曼陀林。1925 年，他成為一所公學校的老師。後來他在東京的音樂學校學作曲理論，1930 年回到台灣。
1933 年，他 28 歲，古倫美亞唱片公司請他當專任作曲家，同一年他寫了〈望春風〉、〈月夜愁〉這些歌。他最有名的四首歌合稱「四月望雨」：〈雨夜花〉、〈望春風〉、〈月夜愁〉、〈四季紅〉。1940 年，他離開唱片業，回去教書，在新竹的一所學校。
客家委員會說，他留下近一百首歌，其中許多到今天還有人唱。〈望春風〉被選為台灣最受歡迎的百年老歌。中文維基百科描述這首歌的旋律採用五聲的「宮」調式。但詞是誰寫的？〈望春風〉的詞是李臨秋寫的，〈雨夜花〉的詞是周添旺寫的。一首歌常常有作曲家和作詞的人，他們是不同的人。
〈雨夜花〉一開始是一首叫〈春天〉的兒歌，是作家廖漢臣 1933 年為台灣的孩子寫的，他交給鄧雨賢譜曲。鄧雨賢的許多歌後來被禁，有些被改寫成日文。一張以為已經遺失的日本流行歌唱片，2007 年被一位收藏者重新發現。有一顆小行星 255989 Dengyushian 用他的名字命名。
為什麼我們這裡不播他的旋律、也不印他的歌詞？台灣的著作權法保護一件作品在作者生存期間，與死後五十年，期間以那一年的最後一天為止。依這條規則，1944 年去世的作曲家，作品在 1995 年就已經不在保護期內，但作詞的人活得比較久，所以歌詞還在保護期內。錄音與編曲各有自己的期間。作曲家的人格權，例如署名的權利、不被歪曲作品的權利，在他死後仍然繼續。所以這一課告訴你事實和歌名，旋律你自己寫。
questions: What is a pentatonic scale?
Why does this lesson not print the words of the songs?
Who wrote the music and who wrote the words of “Longing for the Spring Breeze”?
answers: It is a scale with five notes per octave. Starting on C, the notes are C, D, E, G, and A.
The lyricists lived longer than the composer, and the copyright rule protects a work for the author’s life plus 50 years. So their words are still protected.
Teng Yu-hsien wrote the music, and Li Lin-chiu wrote the words.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It · 動手試試

parts.text_en: A tune that climbs, and ends on the home note, C.
parts.text_zh: 一段往上爬、結束在主音 C 的旋律。

parts.text_en: A tune that rises and falls like a wave.
parts.text_zh: 像波浪一樣起伏的旋律。

parts.text_en: A small pattern comes back: that is repetition.
parts.text_zh: 一個小圖樣回來：這是重複。

parts.text_en: This tune uses F and B. Listen to the notes that sit a half step apart.
parts.text_zh: 這段旋律用了 F 和 B。聽聽那些相差半音的音。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then write your own tune above, and play the game below.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後在上面寫你自己的旋律，再玩下面的遊戲。

oddq.en: Which Note Is Not in the Scale?
oddq.zh: 哪一個音不在五聲音階裡？
oddq.lead_en: Six questions. Each one shows five notes. Four are from the five-note scale C, D, E, G, A. One is not. Find it. You can answer without sound, by looking at the names.
oddq.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題有五個音。其中四個是五聲音階 C、D、E、G、A 的音，一個不是。把它找出來。沒有聲音也能玩，看音名就可以答。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The curriculum names creating melodies, composers, Taiwanese songs, and modes. The words pentatonic and Taiwanese music do not appear in it, but creating and composers do.
curric.lead_zh: 課綱寫到曲調創作、作曲家、臺灣歌謠與調式。「五聲」「臺灣音樂」這些詞課綱裡沒有出現，但「創作」和「作曲家」有。

items.note_en: Writing a tune is melody creation.
items.note_zh: 寫旋律就是曲調創作。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 器樂曲與聲樂曲，如：各國民謠、本土與傳統音樂、古典與流行音樂等，以及樂曲之作曲家、演奏者、傳統藝師與創作背景。
items.note_en: Composers and the background of a song.
items.note_zh: 作曲家與歌曲的創作背景。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 器樂曲與聲樂曲，如：獨奏曲、臺灣歌謠、藝術歌曲，以及樂曲之創作背景或歌詞內涵。
items.note_en: Taiwanese songs, and the background of a song.
items.note_zh: 臺灣歌謠，與歌曲的創作背景。

items.area: 藝術領域・音樂（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 相關音樂語彙，如曲調、調式等描述音樂元素之音樂術語，或相關之一般性用語。
items.note_en: A mode is a set of notes a tune uses, like our five notes.
items.note_zh: 調式是旋律用的一組音，像我們的五個音。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音符背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A teacher, two names on a song, hard years, and whose song it is
culture_cards.title_zh: 一位老師、一首歌上的兩個名字、艱難的年代，和歌是誰的
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about Teng Yu-hsien and his songs. We only write what the sources say.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於鄧雨賢與他的歌的四個小故事。我們只寫來源說的。

cards.body_en: Teng Yu-hsien was born in the Longtan area of Taoyuan and entered the Taipei Normal School at fifteen. He played the cello, the violin, the piano, and the mandolin. He became a teacher at a public school in 1925, left the record industry in 1940, and went back to teaching in Xinzhu. In 2014 a picture book about him was written so that children could get to know him.
cards.body_zh: 鄧雨賢出生在桃園龍潭一帶，十五歲進了臺北師範學校。他會拉大提琴、小提琴，也會彈鋼琴和曼陀林。他 1925 年成為一所公學校的老師，1940 年離開唱片業，回新竹教書。2014 年有人寫了一本關於他的繪本，讓孩子認識他。

cards.body_en: On the songs “Longing for the Spring Breeze” and “Rainy Night Flower”, the music is by Teng Yu-hsien, and the words are by two other people: Li Lin-chiu and Chou Tien-wang. “Rainy Night Flower” began as a children’s song called “Spring”, written in 1933 by Liao Han-chen, and Teng set it to music. So behind one song there may be several people, and each of them has a name that should be remembered.
cards.body_zh: 〈望春風〉和〈雨夜花〉這兩首歌，曲是鄧雨賢寫的，詞是另外兩個人寫的：李臨秋和周添旺。〈雨夜花〉一開始是一首叫〈春天〉的兒歌，1933 年廖漢臣寫的，鄧雨賢為它譜曲。所以一首歌背後可能有好幾個人，每一個人的名字都值得記得。

cards.en: Banned songs, and a lost record
cards.zh: 被禁的歌，與一張失落的唱片
cards.body_en: Many of the songs Teng composed were banned, and some were rewritten into Japanese. This happened in the years when Taiwan was under Japanese rule. Years after his death, in 2007, a record of a Japanese popular song that had been thought lost was rediscovered by a collector. Music can be lost, and it can be found again.
cards.body_zh: 鄧雨賢作曲的許多歌曲曾被禁，有些被改寫成日文。這發生在台灣被日本統治的年代。他去世多年後，2007 年，一張以為已經遺失的日本流行歌唱片，被一位收藏者重新發現。音樂可以遺失，也可以被重新找到。

cards.body_en: Taiwan’s law says a work is protected for the author’s life and 50 years after death, and the term ends on the last day of that year. Using this rule, a composer who died in 1944 is out of copyright from 1995, while a lyricist who died in 1979 is protected through 2029, and one who died in 1988 through 2038. Recordings and performances have their own term, counted from publication. If you ever want to use a song, ask a teacher or an expert first.
cards.body_zh: 台灣的法律說，一件作品在作者生存期間與死後五十年受保護，期間到那一年的最後一天為止。用這條規則算，1944 年去世的作曲家，從 1995 年起不在保護期內；1979 年去世的作詞者，保護到 2029 年；1988 年去世的，保護到 2038 年。錄音與表演有自己的期間，從發表後算。如果你想使用一首歌，先問老師或專家。

myths.myth_en: A song has just one author.
myths.myth_zh: 一首歌只有一個作者。
myths.fact_en: Often one person writes the music and another writes the words. In “Longing for the Spring Breeze”, they were Teng Yu-hsien and Li Lin-chiu.
myths.fact_zh: 常常是一個人寫曲，另一個人寫詞。〈望春風〉是鄧雨賢和李臨秋。

myths.myth_en: Teng Yu-hsien wrote only four songs.
myths.myth_zh: 鄧雨賢只寫了四首歌。
myths.fact_en: Four songs are grouped together as his best known. The Hakka Affairs Council says he left behind nearly 100 songs.
myths.fact_zh: 有四首歌合稱他最有名的。客家委員會說，他留下近一百首歌。

myths.myth_en: When a work is out of copyright, you can do anything with it.
myths.myth_zh: 作品過了著作權期間，就可以隨便使用。
myths.fact_en: Moral rights, such as the right to be named and to keep a work from being distorted, continue after death. Recordings and lyrics have their own terms.
myths.fact_zh: 人格權，例如署名的權利與不被歪曲作品的權利，在死後仍然繼續。錄音與歌詞各有自己的期間。

myths.myth_en: The pentatonic scale belongs to one country.
myths.myth_zh: 五聲音階屬於某一個國家。
myths.fact_en: Many ancient civilizations developed pentatonic scales independently, and they occur in many musical traditions.
myths.fact_zh: 許多古老的文明各自獨立發展出五聲音階，它出現在許多音樂傳統裡。

tricks.title_en: Five notes: C D E G A
tricks.title_zh: 五個音：C D E G A
tricks.body_en: No two are a half step apart.
tricks.body_zh: 任兩個都不相差半音。

tricks.body_en: Often two different people.
tricks.body_zh: 常常是兩個不同的人。

tricks.body_en: Taiwan’s copyright term for a person.
tricks.body_zh: 台灣對個人作者的著作權期間。

tricks.body_en: Facts and names: yes. Others’ tunes: ask first.
tricks.body_zh: 事實與名字：可以。別人的旋律：先問。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，音量不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: When you play the half-step notes F and B, they may sound sharper than the rest. Lower the volume if they bother you.
safety.zh: 播放相差半音的 F 和 B 時，它們可能比其他的音更刺耳。如果覺得不舒服，就把音量調小。

materials.en: A xylophone, a keyboard, or bars with only C, D, E, G, and A
materials.zh: 木琴、鍵盤，或只有 C、D、E、G、A 的音條

materials.en: Paper and a pen
materials.zh: 紙和筆

steps.en: Work in groups. Choose eight notes from C, D, E, G, and A. Write them down.
steps.zh: 分組。從 C、D、E、G、A 選八個音，寫下來。

steps.en: Play your tune. Try to end on C. Does it feel finished?
steps.zh: 彈你的旋律。試著結束在 C。有結束的感覺嗎？

steps.en: Bring back a small pattern. Can your friends hear it?
steps.zh: 讓一個小圖樣回來。同學聽得出來嗎？

steps.en: Swap tunes with another group, and play each other’s tunes.
steps.zh: 和另一組交換旋律，彼此演奏。

activities.tip_en: There is no wrong tune on five notes. Talk about what each tune does.
activities.tip_zh: 五個音上沒有錯的旋律。討論每一段旋律做了什麼。

materials.en: A song your family or class likes
materials.zh: 你的家人或班上喜歡的一首歌

materials.en: A teacher, a family member, or a library to help you look up the names
materials.zh: 老師、家人或圖書館，幫你查名字

steps.en: Choose a song. Find out who wrote the music and who wrote the words.
steps.zh: 選一首歌，查是誰作曲、誰作詞。

steps.en: Write the names and the song’s title on a card. Do not copy the words.
steps.zh: 把名字和歌名寫在卡片上。不要抄歌詞。

steps.en: Ask: how long ago did they live? Is the song still protected?
steps.zh: 問：他們生活在多久以前？這首歌還在保護期內嗎？

steps.en: Share the cards. Say thank you to the people who made the song.
steps.zh: 分享卡片。對寫這首歌的人說謝謝。

activities.tip_en: A teacher or a librarian can help you check. Do not record or share a song without asking.
activities.tip_zh: 老師或圖書館員可以幫你確認。沒有問過，不要錄音，也不要分享歌曲。

sources.zh: 鄧雨賢（1906年7月21日～1944年6月11日），是一位出身台灣桃園龍潭地區的客家作曲家
sources.src: 國家文化記憶庫（文化部）「鄧雨賢」

sources.en: A pentatonic scale is a musical scale with five notes per octave; pentatonic scales were developed independently by many ancient civilizations and are still used in various musical styles; the major pentatonic scale: C, D, E, G, A; the black keys on a piano keyboard comprise a pentatonic scale
sources.zh: 五聲音階是每個八度有五個音的音階；許多古老文明各自獨立發展出五聲音階，至今仍用在各種風格；大調五聲音階：C、D、E、G、A；鋼琴的黑鍵組成一個五聲音階

sources.en: A pentatonic scale picks five notes within an octave; the Chinese pentatonic scale is the best known; traditional Japanese music and Scottish folk songs also use it
sources.zh: 五聲音階是指在一個八度內，選取其中的五個音所排列而成的音階；中國五聲音階最廣為人認識；日本的傳統樂曲、蘇格蘭民謠等也有運用五聲音階
sources.src: 中文維基百科「五聲音階」

sources.en: Five tones: in ancient Chinese music, the five notes gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu. To compose: to make a piece of music. Copyright: includes moral rights and property rights
sources.zh: 五音：中國古代音樂指宮、商、角、徵、羽五個音階。作曲：製作樂曲。著作權：包含著作人格權與著作財產權
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「五音」「作曲」「著作權」

sources.en: Art. 30: property rights last for the author’s life and 50 years after death. Art. 35: the term ends on the last day of the year it expires. Art. 34: recordings and performances last 50 years from publication. Art. 18: moral rights are protected as if the author were alive
sources.zh: 第30條：著作財產權，除本法另有規定外，存續於著作人之生存期間及其死亡後五十年。第35條：期間以屆滿當年之末日為期間之終止。第34條：錄音及表演之著作財產權存續至著作公開發表後五十年。第18條：著作人死亡者，著作人格權之保護視同生存
sources.src: 全國法規資料庫《著作權法》

sources.en: Taiwan's 12-year curriculum: arts (music) 音 E-Ⅲ-5 (曲調創作), 音 A-Ⅲ-1 (作曲家), 音 A-Ⅱ-1 (臺灣歌謠), 音 A-Ⅲ-2 (調式)
sources.zh: 十二年國民基本教育課程綱要藝術領域：音 E-Ⅲ-5（曲調創作）、音 A-Ⅲ-1（作曲家）、音 A-Ⅱ-1（臺灣歌謠）、音 A-Ⅲ-2（調式）
sources.src: 國家教育研究院，十二年國教藝術領域課綱

sources.en: Safe listening: headphone volume to 60% of maximum, personal audio devices less than one hour a day
sources.zh: 安全聆聽：耳機音量不超過最大的 60%、個人音響裝置每天少於一小時
